UAPSDebugHelper.name: UAPSDebugHelper
UAPSDebugHelper.doc:
Squad testing tools. Each one returns a report as text (one line per finding), also
written to the Output Log at Verbose level (LogAdvancedPerception); nothing is drawn on screen.
Show the report however you like: Print String, a widget, the APS Visualizer's panel.

To follow perception events live, bind them in Blueprint, or turn on the APS
Visualizer (APS Core > Show Visualizer), whose event list shows every one.

UAPSEnvironmentComponent.name: UAPSEnvironmentComponent
UAPSEnvironmentComponent.doc:
A place where perception works differently.

The world's effect on the senses used to be one global state on the subsystem:
one light level, one rain intensity, one wind for the entire map. That models
day and night and nothing else — a smoke grenade, a noisy market and a sealed
basement all had to be the same weather as the field outside.

Attach this to anything with a position and it becomes a sphere where the rules
change. Overlapping volumes resolve by Priority, so a smoke cloud inside a dark
warehouse behaves the way you would expect.

Every override is individually opt-in. A volume that only sets Hearing Range
Scale changes nothing else, so a busy market does not accidentally become dark.

FAPSMemory.name: FAPSMemory
FAPSMemory.doc: One remembered thing. Every field except Tag is optional — use what fits.

FAPSMemorySubject.name: FAPSMemorySubject
FAPSMemorySubject.doc:
What a memory is about.

Any belief subject qualifies — a person, a place, an object. "I remember
something happened here" is the same mechanism as "I remember him", which is
why this is a subject rather than an actor pointer.

Build one with Make Actor Subject or Make Place Subject.

FAPSSenseSample.name: FAPSSenseSample
FAPSSenseSample.doc:
One sense's contribution, flattened for a policy to reason about.

Deliberately small. A policy is called once per target per tick, so this is
copied often; passing the full belief record would move roughly thirty times
as much memory for data fusion does not use.

UAPSFusionPolicy.name: UAPSFusionPolicy
UAPSFusionPolicy.doc:
How several senses become one number.

The shipped rule is "the best active sense sets the floor, each additional
active sense adds a flat corroboration bonus". That deliberately never lets a
silent sense drag confidence down, but it also means two weak corroborating
senses can never beat one strong one — which some games want and some do not.

Override Fuse Confidence to decide it yourself.

UAPSThreatPolicy.name: UAPSThreatPolicy
UAPSThreatPolicy.doc:
How dangerous a target is, as a score in [0..1].

The shipped rule weighs confidence, damage taken, how many senses agree, the
relationship and whether the target is closing. A stealth game might care only
about whether the target has seen the AI back; a horror game might make an
unarmed civilian the most threatening thing in the level.

The threat LEVEL is still derived from the profile's thresholds, so a policy
only has to answer the interesting half.

UAPSAttentionPolicy.name: UAPSAttentionPolicy
UAPSAttentionPolicy.doc:
Which target the AI commits to.

The shipped rule keeps the highest-scoring target and refuses to switch until
the stickiness window has passed AND a challenger beats it by a margin — which
stops flicker but is not always what a game wants. A boss might always turn to
whoever last hurt it; a guard dog might always chase the nearest thing.

UAPSQualityProfile.name: UAPSQualityProfile
UAPSQualityProfile.doc:
Runtime cost controls, applied on top of a perception profile.

WHY IT EXISTS
  Scaling an agent's cost used to mean swapping its profile for a cheaper one,
  which rebuilt every sense and reset the ledger, emotions and attention. An AI
  throttled mid-chase forgot who it was chasing. That is the wrong trade: cost
  and behaviour are different axes and should be set independently.

  A quality profile only scales how *often* and how *finely* perception runs.
  It never changes ranges, thresholds, fairness or lifecycle timing, so an agent
  can be made cheaper or more expensive at any moment without losing a single
  thing it believes.

SETUP
  Optional. With none assigned every multiplier is 1.0 and nothing changes.
  Assign one on the component, or call Set Quality Profile at runtime — from a
  scalability setting, a platform check, or your own significance logic.

NOTE
  Deliberately does NOT expose max tracked targets. Changing ledger capacity
  means reallocating belief slots, which is exactly the destructive reset this
  asset exists to avoid. Put that on the profile.

UAPSSignificancePolicy.name: UAPSSignificancePolicy
UAPSSignificancePolicy.doc:
Deliberately NOT Abstract, unlike the fusion, threat and attention policies.
Those are pure hooks that are only ever instantiated when a profile names a
concrete subclass. This one carries the shipping rule and is instantiated as
itself when nobody overrides it — and allocating an abstract class outside the
editor asserts, so marking it Abstract worked in PIE and crashed on launch in a
packaged build.

UAPSTargetComponent.name: UAPSTargetComponent
UAPSTargetComponent.doc:
Add this to anything AI should be able to SEE properly — the player, NPCs,
vehicles, props.

WHY IT EXISTS
  Epic's perception traces exactly one ray, to the target's capsule centre.
  Stand behind a waist-high crate with your head fully exposed and the AI
  reports "not seen", because the one ray it casts is blocked. This component
  gives the AI a set of points to trace against instead — head, chest, pelvis,
  shoulders, or whatever you choose — and the result becomes a percentage
  exposed rather than a yes/no.

SETUP — the whole thing is optional
  Add the component and you get sensible defaults immediately. Nothing else
  is required: with no component at all, the profile's DefaultVisibilitySamples
  are used, so existing content keeps working unchanged.

  To tune it: fill VisibilitySamples with socket names from your skeleton.
  Sockets are resolved against the owner's skeletal mesh every evaluation, so
  they follow animation — a target leaning out of cover really does expose
  its head.

STANCE
  Set Stance from your movement code (or tick bAutoDetectStance and let the
  component read the character's crouch state). Stance decides how many points
  must be visible before the target counts as seen, so a crouched target
  behind cover stays hidden longer than a standing one.

LIGHT
  Set LightLevelOverride from your lighting/light-gem code for exact control,
  or leave it at -1 and let the perception profile's sun-shadow trace decide.

UAPSViewLibrary.name: UAPSViewLibrary
UAPSViewLibrary.doc:
World-level "APS|View" nodes: which AI to show in detail, and the Visualizer switch.
Per-AI view nodes are on the APS Core (Get Vision Fans, Get Sample Points, ...).

FAPSViewFan.name: FAPSViewFan
FAPSViewFan.doc:
One view cone as a flat shape: where vision gets to along each direction.

Apex plus Rim is a triangle fan. Each rim point is where sight stops along its
direction: at a wall, past glass as far as vision gets through, at full range
in the open. So the shape is what the AI can see, not just its settings.

FAPSViewPoint.name: FAPSViewPoint
FAPSViewPoint.doc: One of vision's sample points on a target.

FAPSHeardSound.name: FAPSHeardSound
FAPSHeardSound.doc: One sound, as one AI heard it.

FAPSSenseRanges.name: FAPSSenseRanges
FAPSSenseRanges.doc: How far each of an AI's senses reaches right now (cm). 0 for a sense it does not have.

FEmotionalState.name: FEmotionalState
FEmotionalState.doc:
Per-agent emotional state. Five independent float channels [0..1].
Driven by perception events. Configured by PerceptionProfile.

UPerceptionProfile.name: UPerceptionProfile
UPerceptionProfile.doc:
Data asset defining all perception parameters for one AI archetype.
Swap at runtime to instantly change how the AI perceives the world.

SECTION GUIDE — open only what you need:
  Senses|Setup    — which senses exist, weights, tick rates
  Ranges          — how far each sense reaches
  Detection       — how each sense identifies targets (angles, thresholds, accumulation)
  Loss            — how long before each sense loses a target
  Fusion          — how multiple senses combine into one confidence value
  Memory          — how long the AI remembers targets after losing them
  Awareness       — confidence thresholds for Suspect / Detect / Track
  Attention       — which target the AI commits focus to
  Spatial         — position prediction and uncertainty
  Performance     — tick rate, max targets
  Brain|Emotions  — fear, aggression, curiosity, panic
  Brain|Threat    — how threat level is calculated
  Brain|Squad     — intel sharing with squadmates
  Brain|PlayerModel — learning from player behavior

UPerceptionSoundSystem.name: UPerceptionSoundSystem
UPerceptionSoundSystem.doc:
Static function library for emitting sounds into the Advanced Perception System.

HOW TO USE (Blueprint):
  On footstep anim notify -> EmitSound(Self, Self, DA_Sound_Footstep)
  On explosion -> EmitSoundAtLocation(Self, HitLocation, DA_Sound_Explosion)

HOW TO USE (C++):
  UPerceptionSoundSystem::EmitSound(this, this, FootstepAsset);

No component needed. No manual loudness or range values at the call site.
Only AI agents within SoundType->MaxRange will be notified.

FAPSProfileOverride.name: FAPSProfileOverride
FAPSProfileOverride.doc:
One changed number, named by property.

The composition system needs a way to say "this profile, but with a longer
vision range" without duplicating an asset that has 170 fields on it. Where a
child asset exists the difference can be read off the asset itself, but a
per-agent tweak has no asset to diff against, so it is expressed as a list of
these instead.

Property is the exact name as it appears on the profile, e.g. "VisionMaxRange".
Names that do not resolve are reported by Validate Profile and logged once at
composition time rather than failing silently.

FFloatArray.name: FFloatArray
FFloatArray.doc: Wrapper so TMap can hold a TArray<float> as its value type in a UPROPERTY.

FAPSLocationObservation.name: FAPSLocationObservation
FAPSLocationObservation.doc:
One non-actor observation a sense produced this tick.

Senses return these from CollectLocationObservations(); the core turns them
into Location beliefs. This is what stops an anonymous stimulus from having to
borrow an actor's belief record.

FAPSVisibilitySample.name: FAPSVisibilitySample
FAPSVisibilitySample.doc:
One ray sample against a target, used for percentage-exposed visibility.
Resolved from a mesh socket when available, otherwise from a local-space offset.

FAPSReplicatedTargetState.name: FAPSReplicatedTargetState
FAPSReplicatedTargetState.doc:
Compact per-target perception state replicated to clients.
Perception itself stays server-authoritative — this exists so client UI
(detection meters, spectator overlays) can read derived state without
every project hand-rolling its own replication.

FPerceptionEpisode.name: FPerceptionEpisode
FPerceptionEpisode.doc:
A record of one past engagement with a specific target.
Written when target goes Lost from Detected or Tracked.
Stored in FBeliefRecord.Episodes (ring buffer, max APS_MAX_EPISODES).

USAGE IN BEHAVIOR TREES:
  PerceptionCore → GetRecentEpisodes(Target) → Array of FPerceptionEpisode
  Then query: How was target lost last time? Where? How long was the engagement?
  Example: Last 3 losses were all Occluded at similar positions → bias search there.

FPerceptionSenseResult.name: FPerceptionSenseResult
FPerceptionSenseResult.doc:
What one sense reports about one target each time it is evaluated. A sense fills in Is Active, Confidence,
 Estimated Location, Location Accuracy, Raw Signal Strength and Sense ID (a Blueprint sense with Make Perception
 Sense Result in Evaluate, which is why those six are writable); the rest are vision's details.

FAPSPerceptionFrame.name: FAPSPerceptionFrame
FAPSPerceptionFrame.doc:
One target's belief at one moment, as recorded.

Perception bugs are temporal: the frame that explains the problem is always
the one that has just gone past. A recording keeps the last few seconds so the
interesting frame can be looked at after the fact instead of being chased with
a breakpoint.

Deliberately small. This is written every tick for every tracked target, so a
field that is merely interesting costs memory on every agent in the level.

URelationshipComponent.name: URelationshipComponent
URelationshipComponent.doc:
Per-AI relationship rules. Add to AI Pawn alongside UPerceptionCore.
Stores team-based and class-based relationship mappings.
Optional — if not present, all relationships default to Unknown.

USenseUnit.name: USenseUnit
USenseUnit.doc:
Abstract base class for all perception senses.

PIPELINE CONTRACT — PerceptionCore calls these methods in order every tick:
  1. PreTick(DeltaTime, Profile)          — once per AI, before target loop
  2. Evaluate(Context, Profile, Target)   — once per target
  3. GetSenseDelegatePayload(...)         — fired if sense is active
  4. PostTickFlush()                      — cleanup after all targets processed

PerceptionCore NEVER casts to a specific sense type.
All sense-specific behavior lives in the sense class itself.

TO ADD A NEW SENSE:
  1. Subclass USenseUnit in C++ or Blueprint
  2. Override GetSenseID_Implementation()
  3. Override Evaluate_Implementation()
  4. Override GetSenseDelegatePayload() to return which delegate fires
  5. Add to PerceptionProfile SenseClasses array
  Done. No changes to PerceptionCore, MemoryEngine, or any other system.

FHearingSoundEvent.name: FHearingSoundEvent
FHearingSoundEvent.doc:
Lightweight struct representing a single sound stimulus pending evaluation.
Supports both new (SoundType-based) and legacy (direct loudness) paths.

USenseUnit_Hearing.name: USenseUnit_Hearing
USenseUnit_Hearing.doc:
Hearing sense with distance attenuation and wall occlusion.

Detection is ONLY via explicit sound events:
  - New path:    UPerceptionSoundSystem::EmitSound() -> ReportSoundFromType()
  - Legacy path: PerceptionCore::ReportSoundEvent(Loudness, Range) -> ReportSound()

Passive velocity-based detection has been removed.
All sounds must be explicitly reported via the sound system or legacy call.

USenseUnit_Smell.name: USenseUnit_Smell
USenseUnit_Smell.doc:
=====================================================================
SMELL SENSE — Reference Example of a Custom Sense
=====================================================================
This class demonstrates the full custom sense workflow:
  - Subclass USenseUnit in C++ (Evaluate_Implementation + GetSenseID_Implementation)
  - Expose sense-specific parameters as UPROPERTY directly on the sense
    (since PerceptionProfile only covers built-in senses)
  - Override GetDefaultInterval() for an appropriate update rate
  - Override GetMaxSensingRange() so GatherPotentialTargets includes far targets
  - The sense is automatically Blueprint-subclassable (no extra work needed)

HOW SMELL WORKS IN THIS IMPLEMENTATION:
  Smell is a short-to-medium range sense (~400 cm default) that:
    1. Falls off linearly with distance (not inverse-square — smell disperses slowly)
    2. Gets a directional bonus when the target is UPWIND of the perceiver
       (perceiver is downwind, scent travels toward them)
    3. Is blocked by walls (same wall counting as hearing)
    4. Is NOT affected by ambient light (smell works in darkness)
    5. Produces low spatial accuracy (you know ROUGHLY where a scent comes from)

TO USE IN YOUR PROJECT:
  1. Open your PerceptionProfile data asset.
  2. Add Smell Sense (or a Blueprint child of it) to the SenseClasses array.
  3. Optionally give Smell Sense a weight in the SenseWeights map.
  4. Call GetWorld()->GetSubsystem<UAPSSubsystem>()->SetWeatherModifier()
     to simulate rain reducing scent (WeatherMod already read from context).
  5. Set the wind with Set Wind State on the APS subsystem (the way it blows,
     and its speed). SetWindDirection() on the sense overrides it per AI.

TO EXTEND IN BLUEPRINT:
  1. Create a Blueprint class inheriting from SenseUnit_Smell.
  2. Override the Evaluate event to add custom logic (e.g. scent masking items).
  3. Or just use this class directly with adjusted UPROPERTY defaults.

TO EXTEND IN C++:
  1. Subclass this class or USenseUnit directly.
  2. Override Evaluate_Implementation() and GetSenseID_Implementation().
=====================================================================

USenseUnit_Touch.name: USenseUnit_Touch
USenseUnit_Touch.doc:
Modular physical contact sense.

Supports:
  - One-shot hits (collision, explosion impact) — instant high confidence
  - Persistent contacts (grab, ongoing overlap) — confidence holds while active
  - Multiple simultaneous contacts — highest priority wins for confidence
  - Physics impulse -> strength mapping via ReportContactWithImpulse()
  - Contact type priority: Explosion > Grab > Collision > Bump

HOW TO USE:
  1. Add USenseUnit_Touch to your Profile's SenseClasses array.
  2. From your AI's OnComponentHit: call PerceptionCore->ReportTouchContact(Other, Collision, 1.0)
  3. From your AI's OnComponentBeginOverlap: call ReportTouchContact(Other, Grab, 1.0, true) [persistent]
  4. From your AI's OnComponentEndOverlap: call EndTouchContact(Other)
  5. From physics hit: call ReportContactWithImpulse(Other, Collision, ImpulseVector)

USenseUnit_Vision.name: USenseUnit_Vision
USenseUnit_Vision.doc:
Vision sense.

Differences from Epic's UAISense_Sight, all configurable on the profile:
  - Multi-point visibility sampling with a continuous 0-1 exposure ratio,
    resolved from mesh sockets so it follows animation. Epic traces once, to
    the capsule centre, and returns a boolean.
  - Stance-dependent minimum visible points — crouching behind cover actually hides you.
  - Separate horizontal and vertical FOV. Epic's cone is perfectly symmetric.
  - Focal, peripheral and rear-motion cones instead of one all-or-nothing cone.
  - Multi-channel occlusion with per-surface transmission, so doors, vehicles,
    pawns and foliage block or dampen sight instead of being ignored.
  - Per-target light sampling rather than a single global ambient value.

UAPSDescriptorLibrary.name: UAPSDescriptorLibrary
UAPSDescriptorLibrary.doc:
Blueprint access to descriptors — building one for Report Observation or Match
Descriptor, and comparing two directly. The struct's own C++ methods are not
reachable from Blueprint, so without these a Blueprint could only assemble a
descriptor by hand from a Make node and an array.

UAPSEvidenceComponent.name: UAPSEvidenceComponent
UAPSEvidenceComponent.doc:
Something left behind that says an event happened here.

A body, blood, a forced lock, tyre marks, a dropped weapon. Add this to an
actor and it becomes perceivable — an AI that sees it forms a belief about the
PLACE, not about the object, because what matters is that something happened
here rather than that a prop exists.

The world keeps this after you have left, which is the point: hiding the body
stops being flavour and starts being a decision.

The AI perceives it as a THING (Subject Kind Object), not someone: its belief
says how well it has seen it (Get Perceived Objects), but it is never a target,
and no On AI Suspect / On AI Detect / On AI See names it. Finding it is an APS
Observer's On Evidence Discovered, and the place belief that raises.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
  It does not decide what finding it means. Discovery raises a location belief
  and writes a memory; whether that starts a manhunt, a shrug or a phone call
  is the developer's logic.

FAPSChannelSpec.name: FAPSChannelSpec
FAPSChannelSpec.doc: What a channel costs the information passing through it.

UAPSKnowledgeSubsystem.name: UAPSKnowledgeSubsystem
UAPSKnowledgeSubsystem.doc:
What a faction knows, as opposed to what any one of its members knows.

The perception kernel gives every agent its own private beliefs, which die with
it. That is correct for an individual and wrong for an organisation: shoot the
only guard who saw you and the crime never happened. This is where knowledge
outlives the knower.

Deliberately not referenced by the kernel. Perception publishes into this;
nothing here reaches back.

UAPSObserverComponent.name: UAPSObserverComponent
UAPSObserverComponent.doc:
Turns one AI's private perception into faction knowledge.

This is the only place the two halves meet, and the meeting is one-way: it
reads the perception component beside it and publishes upward. Perception
itself has no idea this exists, which is what keeps the kernel free of any
notion of factions, witnesses or manhunts.

SETUP
  Add it next to an APS Core, set Faction, done. Whenever the AI becomes
  confident enough about a target it files a report — describing what it could
  actually make out, over the channel you choose.

FAPSSearchPoint.name: FAPSSearchPoint
FAPSSearchPoint.doc: One place worth looking, and how much it is worth.

UAPSSearchComponent.name: UAPSSearchComponent
UAPSSearchComponent.doc:
Where could they be by now?

The kernel answers "where did I last see them" and grows an uncertainty radius
around it — a single number that expands straight through walls, so a target
that ducked into a broom cupboard is modelled as possibly being three rooms
away through solid stone. That radius is why search behaviour built on APS has
been the weakest part of it.

This replaces the number with a field. Probability starts at the last known
position and spreads outward at the speed the target could actually move,
skipping anywhere they could not stand. Cells the AI has physically been near
are emptied, so it stops re-checking rooms it has already cleared, and two
searchers naturally divide the space because whatever one clears is no longer
worth the other's time.

IT NEVER MOVES AN AI. It answers "where is worth looking, in what order" and
stops. Going there is the behaviour tree's job.

UAPSSignatureComponent.name: UAPSSignatureComponent
UAPSSignatureComponent.doc:
What an observer could tell about this actor if it got a good look.

Add it to anyone who can be described — the player, NPCs, vehicles. Without it
an actor simply has no describable features, and observers can only ever know
it as "someone", which is a perfectly reasonable thing for scenery to be.

DISGUISES
  Change a trait and every description built from the old one stops matching.
  That is the whole mechanic: swap Clothing from RedCoat to GuardUniform and
  the manhunt is looking for somebody who no longer exists. Nothing else needs
  to know it happened.

FAPSTrait.name: FAPSTrait
FAPSTrait.doc:
One observable fact about someone.

Identity in the perception kernel is pointer equality — the AI either knows an
actor or it does not, and no disguise can change that. Traits are the layer
that makes identity something you can be partly right about: an observer
collects what it could actually make out, and matching that against known
people is a separate, fallible step.

Observability is what makes recognition progressive. A coat colour reads across
a courtyard; a face does not. Setting it honestly is what produces "a person in
a red coat" at distance and "that is Marcus" up close, from the same data.

FAPSDescriptor.name: FAPSDescriptor
FAPSDescriptor.doc:
A set of traits — either what somebody actually is, or what a witness managed
to make out. The same type serves both, which is what lets one be matched
against the other.

EAPSViewFanKind.name: EAPSViewFanKind
EAPSViewFanKind.doc: Which of an AI's view cones a fan is.

EAPSViewPointState.name: EAPSViewPointState
EAPSViewPointState.doc: How much of vision reaches one of a target's sample points.

EAPSBeliefSubject.name: EAPSBeliefSubject
EAPSBeliefSubject.doc:
What a belief is *about*.

Until now a belief always pointed at an AActor, which meant the AI could only
believe in things it could already name. "Someone is in that room", "a gunshot
came from the bank", "there is a body here" had nowhere to live — and an
anonymous stimulus had to be scored against whichever actor happened to be
under evaluation, which is how one explosion made a guard suspicious of three
unrelated bystanders at once.

Actor is the original case and still the default, so nothing that existed
before behaves differently.

EAPSPerceptionBlocker.name: EAPSPerceptionBlocker
EAPSPerceptionBlocker.doc:
Why a sense produced nothing this evaluation.

"The AI can't see me and I don't know why" is the single most common question
a perception system gets asked. The pipeline already knows the answer at every
early return — it just used to throw it away.

EAPSEyeDirectionMode.name: EAPSEyeDirectionMode
EAPSEyeDirectionMode.doc:
Where the vision cone's DIRECTION comes from.

Epic's AIPerception always uses the controller's control rotation, which has no
connection to the skeletal mesh — head turns, aim offsets and lean animations
never move the cone. These modes let you bind facing to what the mesh is
actually doing.

EAPSEyeSocketAlignment.name: EAPSEyeSocketAlignment
EAPSEyeSocketAlignment.doc:
How the eye socket's rotation is turned into a look direction.

A bone's local axes are arbitrary — on Epic's mannequin the head bone's X axis
runs UP the neck, so binding a vision cone straight to it aims the AI at the
sky. Sockets can carry a corrective rotation, but only if whoever made them
bothered to orient it.

EAPSArchetype.name: EAPSArchetype
EAPSArchetype.doc:
Ready-made starting points for the kinds of AI people build most.

These exist to prove the kernel is genre-blind as much as to save time: four
very different AI over one unchanged core, each of them nothing but values on
an ordinary profile.

EAPSStance.name: EAPSStance
EAPSStance.doc:
Target posture. Drives how many visibility sample points must be exposed
before the target counts as seen (Splinter Cell's stance-dependent bone
threshold) — a crouched target behind cover needs fewer visible points to
stay hidden than a standing one.

EAPSVisionCone.name: EAPSVisionCone
EAPSVisionCone.doc: Which vision cone produced a detection. Reported on the sense result.

EAPSCommsChannel.name: EAPSCommsChannel
EAPSCommsChannel.doc:
How a report reached the faction.

Squad sharing in the kernel is instant, lossless and range-gated, which makes
every AI on a team effectively telepathic. These are the routes information
actually travels by, each with its own cost — and the reason silencing a
witness before they reach a radio is a real tactic rather than a cosmetic one.

FOnAITelegraph.name: FOnAITelegraph
FOnAITelegraph.doc: Fires before full alert so the player can read that they are about to be spotted.

FOnAPSReplicatedStateChanged.name: FOnAPSReplicatedStateChanged
FOnAPSReplicatedStateChanged.doc: Fires on clients when the replicated perception summary changes.

FOnAPSLocationBelief.name: FOnAPSLocationBelief
FOnAPSLocationBelief.doc:
Fires when a belief that is NOT about an actor changes lifecycle state — a
noise with no author, a discovered object.

Deliberately a separate delegate rather than passing null through the existing
actor events: every OnAISuspect handler ever written assumes a valid Target,
and quietly starting to hand them nullptr would break content that has no idea
this feature exists.

FOnAttentionChanged.name: FOnAttentionChanged
FOnAttentionChanged.doc:
Fires when the AI's attention shifts to a different primary target.
OldTarget may be null (attention acquired for the first time).
NewTarget is the new focus — never null when this fires.
Use in BT to cancel current pursuit and re-plan for the new target.

FOnAIPainReported.name: FOnAIPainReported
FOnAIPainReported.doc:
Fires when ReportPainFromDefinition() is called.
 PainDef = the DataAsset describing this pain type. PainLevel = accumulated 0-1.

FOnAIDamaged.name: FOnAIDamaged
FOnAIDamaged.doc:
Fires on every damage event received by the AI owner (ApplyDamage, ApplyRadialDamage, ApplyPointDamage).
 Developer decides what to do: call ReportPain, SetTargetConfidence, or ignore.

functions.name: GetAPSHealthFraction
functions.doc:
Remaining health as a fraction, 1 for untouched and 0 for dead.
Values outside that range are clamped.

functions.name: GetAPSStance
functions.doc: Current posture.

functions.name: SquadStateReport
functions.doc:
Agent's squad: its Squad ID, every member, their distance to Agent, whether they are
in share range, and their combat role. Run it on one AI to check a squad is wired up.

functions.name: SimulateSquadShare
functions.doc:
Hand Sender's belief about Target to Receiver, as a squad share would, without Receiver
having to perceive anything. Sender must hold a belief about Target. Tests the share
pipeline with one pair of AI.

functions.name: SimulateSquadAlert
functions.doc: Fire On AI Squad Alert on Receiver, to test its response to an alert in isolation.

functions.name: TraceSquadSharePath
functions.doc:
Why a share from Sender would or would not reach each squad member, step by step:
Squad ID set, belief held, Min Threat To Share met, members registered, each in range.
A dry run: nothing is shared.

functions.name: SquadBeliefsReport
functions.doc: What every member of Agent's squad believes about Target. Run it after a share to see it landed.

functions.name: ForceFullSquadShare
functions.doc: Share Sender's belief about Target with every squad member, ignoring range and Min Threat To Share.

functions.name: FuseConfidence
ScoreThreat
SelectAttentionTarget
ScoreSignificance
GetEffectiveStance
functions.doc: Resolve the stance in effect right now, honouring bAutoDetectStance.

functions.name: GetFocusAgent
functions.doc:
The AI to show in full detail: the nearest one the player's camera can see (in front of
it, nothing solid between the camera and the top of its head), or the nearest one when
none is in view. Only Visualized: consider only AIs with Show Visualizer on.

functions.name: IsAgentInCameraView
functions.doc: True when the player's camera can see this AI: in front of it, nothing solid in between (glass and foliage its profile sees through do not count).

functions.name: GetFeetLocation
functions.doc: The floor under an actor: its location minus its collision half height. For drawing on the floor under an AI or a target.

functions.name: GetHeadLocation
functions.doc: The top of an actor's collision: where a label over its head goes.

functions.name: GetAllAgents
functions.doc: Every APS Core in the world.

functions.name: GetVisualizerMode
functions.doc:
What the APS Visualizer shows: 0 nothing, 1 everything (the default), 2 status only
(each AI's state over its head, no cones or rings). The console variable aps.Visualizer.

functions.name: GetVisualizerPage
functions.doc: The page the Visualizer's screen panel shows (0 Senses ... ). The console variable aps.VisualizerPage.

functions.name: GetSourceProfile
functions.doc:
The profile asset as assigned, before inheritance and overrides.

Profile is the resolved result the agent actually reads. When neither the
asset nor this agent overrides anything the two are the same object.

functions.name: SetProfileNumber
functions.doc:
Set one numeric profile value for this agent alone, at runtime.

Property is the exact name from the Details panel with spaces removed, e.g.
"VisionMaxRange". Returns false and logs when the name does not resolve.
Nothing the agent believes is reset — the new value is read on the next tick.

functions.name: SetProfileFlag
functions.doc: As Set Profile Number, for a checkbox.

functions.name: GetProfileNumber
functions.doc: Read a numeric profile value by name. Returns Fallback if it does not resolve.

functions.name: ClearProfileOverrides
functions.doc: Drop every per-agent override and go back to the profile as authored.

functions.name: SetQualityProfile
functions.doc:
Swap the quality profile at runtime. Safe at any moment: no sense is
 rebuilt, no belief is discarded. Pass none to return to full quality.

functions.name: SetShowVisualizer
functions.doc: Show or remove this AI's Visualizer now.

functions.name: GetVisualizer
functions.doc: This AI's Visualizer actor, while it is shown.

functions.name: GetAttentionTarget
functions.doc:
Returns the current attention target — the single target the AI is
committing its full focus to. This is what Behavior Trees should use
for chase, attack, and search decisions.

Different from GetTopTarget() (which returns highest sort score this tick).
This returns the attention-locked target, which persists through
AttentionStickinessTime even if a slightly higher-scored target appears.
Only a target the AI has noticed (Suspected or more) takes attention. It can
still be one the AI only suspects, so check its state before chasing it.

functions.name: GetAttentionDuration
functions.doc:
Returns how long (seconds) the AI has been focused on the current
attention target. Useful for BT: "have I been chasing this for > 10s?"

functions.name: ForceAttentionTarget
functions.doc:
Force the attention target immediately, bypassing stickiness.
Use when an event should override current focus — e.g. player fires
a shot directly at this AI, player enters a trigger zone.

functions.name: GetTopTarget
functions.doc: Returns the top-scoring target this tick among those the AI has noticed (may differ from attention target).

functions.name: GetTargetsSortedByScore
functions.doc:
Beliefs about someone, best first. Things it perceives (APS Evidence, Set
 Perceived As Object) are not targets: see Get Perceived Objects.

functions.name: GetPerceivedObjects
functions.doc:
Beliefs about things rather than someone: a body, a forced lock (APS Evidence,
Set Perceived As Object). Most confident first. Smoothed Confidence says how
well the AI has seen each; Target is the thing itself.

functions.name: GetSenseResult
functions.doc:
Everything one sense reported about a target at its last evaluation. For vision that is
the exposure (how much of the target is visible, 0-1), the visible sample point count,
which cone saw it, the light level it judged, its confidence, and the blocker when it saw
nothing. Use it to show what the AI sees on a HUD or a debug screen.

Senses run on their own intervals, so Is Active drops out between evaluations; use
Was Active Last Eval (or Confidence) to ask "is it perceiving the target right now".

@param SenseID  The sense's ID, e.g. Vision, Hearing, Smell.
@return False when this AI holds no belief about the target or runs no such sense.

functions.name: GetEyeViewPoint
functions.doc:
Where this AI's eyes are and which way they look, as vision uses them.

Location is the eye socket when Use Eye Socket is on, else the actor plus Eye Height
Offset. Forward is the facing from the last update, with Eye Direction Mode and Eye Turn
Rate applied, so it can trail the body. Before the first update it is the actor's facing.
Use it to draw the real cone, aim a head or a flashlight, or check what the AI could see.

functions.name: GetVisionFans
IsLookingAt
functions.doc:
True while vision is looking the target's way: inside one of its cones and in range.
Only then do its sample points mean anything; a clear line to someone outside every
cone only says nothing is in between. Why Not says why not (Outside Cone, Out Of Range;
No Context for an AI without a Vision sense).

functions.name: GetSamplePoints
functions.doc:
Vision's sample points on a target and how much of vision reaches each: the same points
and traces the vision sense uses, from the same eyes. A head over a wall is one Seen
point and four Blocked. Traces once per point, so call it for one target at a time.
@return False when this AI has no Vision sense or there is no target.

functions.name: GetRecentSounds
functions.doc: The sounds this AI heard in the last Max Age seconds, oldest first (see Record Heard Sounds).

functions.name: HasSense
functions.doc: True when this AI runs the sense, e.g. Vision, Hearing, Smell. A profile has ranges for every sense; only the ones in Sense Classes run.

functions.name: GetSenseIDs
functions.doc: The senses this AI runs, in profile order.

functions.name: GetSenseRanges
functions.doc: How far each sense reaches right now, with any zone the AI stands in applied. 0 for a sense it does not run.

functions.name: GetSoundReach
functions.doc: How far a Sound Type carries to this AI right now (cm): its range, scaled by any zone the AI stands in.

functions.name: GetViewTarget
functions.doc:
The target a view of this AI is about: the local player when this AI holds a belief
about them, otherwise its most confident belief that is not a friend or teammate.
None when it believes nothing about anyone.

functions.name: GetLossReason
functions.doc:
Why was this target last lost?
Returns ELossReason::Unknown if target has never been lost or is currently active.
Use in Behavior Trees to drive intelligent search behavior:
  Occluded     → go to LastKnownPosition, search cover
  SoundFaded   → investigate the sound area, don't chase
  ScentLost    → follow LossDirection (scent trail)
  OutOfRange   → move toward LastKnownPosition, expand search
  SensorDropout → short investigation then resume patrol

functions.name: GetLossDirection
functions.doc:
Direction the target was moving when last lost.
Useful for OutOfRange and ScentLost — predict where they went.
Returns ZeroVector if direction unknown.

functions.name: GetRecentEpisodes
functions.doc:
Get the recorded episodes for a target (up to APS_MAX_EPISODES).
Returns false if no episodes exist yet (target never lost).
Episodes are ordered oldest → newest.

Example BT usage:
  GetRecentEpisodes(Target, Episodes)
  → last Episode.HowLost == Occluded at Episodes.Last().LocationWhenLost
  → go search there instead of doing a generic sweep

functions.name: GetLastEpisode
functions.doc:
Returns the most recent episode for a target, or false if none.
Convenience wrapper for the common "what happened last time?" query.

functions.name: ClearEpisodes
functions.doc:
Clear all recorded episodes for a target.
Use when starting a fresh encounter (new game session, target respawned etc.)

functions.name: BroadcastAlertToSquad
functions.doc:
Broadcast a positional alert to all squadmates without sharing full belief data.
Use when you heard something but haven't confirmed a target yet.

functions.name: ReportTouchContact
functions.doc: Call from OnComponentBeginOverlap or OnActorHit.

functions.name: ReportTouchContactWithImpulse
functions.doc: Call from physics OnComponentHit — maps impulse to strength automatically.

functions.name: EndTouchContact
functions.doc: Call from OnComponentEndOverlap to end a persistent contact.

functions.name: ReportPainFromDefinition
functions.doc: Report pain via DataAsset. Always fires OnAIPainReported.

functions.name: ClearPainFromDefinition
functions.doc: Remove pain by DataAsset.

functions.name: ClearAllPain
functions.doc: Remove all pain of all types.

functions.name: SetPainTypeEnabledFromDefinition
functions.display: Set Pain Type Enabled from Definition
functions.doc: Enable or disable a pain type by DataAsset.

functions.name: GetPainLevelFromDefinition
functions.doc: Get current pain level by DataAsset.

functions.name: GetTotalPainLevel
functions.doc: Get combined pain level across all active types (0-1).

functions.name: SetFearInput
functions.doc:
Set external fear input [0..1]. Drive Fear emotion from your game logic
(e.g. horror events, scripted sequences). 0 = no fear input (decays normally).

functions.name: SetTargetConfidence
functions.doc:
Manually set target confidence. Use when you want full control over how
damage or other events build awareness (e.g. bAutoConfidenceFromDamage=false).
Confidence is clamped 0-1 and fed directly into the belief record.

NOTE: this only ever raises belief — it takes the maximum of the current and
supplied value and applies immediately. To lower, cap or clear belief, or to
have the change expire on its own, use Add Target Evidence instead.

functions.name: AddTargetEvidence
RemoveTargetEvidence
functions.doc: Revoke one piece of evidence by tag. Returns true if something was removed.

functions.name: ClearTargetEvidence
functions.doc: Revoke every piece of evidence about a target.

functions.name: GetTargetEvidence
functions.doc: Read the evidence currently held about a target.

functions.name: ReportVibrationEvent
functions.doc: Use for vibration NOT caused by a moving actor (e.g. grenade). Moving actors are detected automatically.

functions.name: SetEmotion
functions.doc:
Manually set an emotion channel [0..1].
Use for scripted sequences, cinematics, or gameplay events.
The engine will continue to drive channels naturally next tick —
call every tick or use SetFearInput() for sustained fear.

functions.name: ResetEmotionalState
functions.doc: Reset all emotion channels to 0 and DominantEmotion to Calm.

functions.name: Debug_ResetDamageTracking
functions.doc: Zero the damage dealt and received on every belief this AI holds.

functions.name: Debug_PrintBeliefState
functions.doc: Write every belief this AI holds to the Output Log.

functions.name: Debug_TogglePause
functions.doc: Flip Pause Perception.

functions.name: GetLODTier
functions.doc: How much detail APS gives this AI right now: 0 full, higher is cheaper (farther from the camera).

functions.name: GetReplicatedPerceptionState
functions.doc:
Read the replicated perception summary.

On the server this is the authoritative state; on clients it is the copy
that replicated with the Pawn. Requires Replicate Perception State on the
profile and Replicates on the Pawn.

functions.name: IsLocationInNeverSearchZone
functions.display: Is Location in Never Search Zone
functions.doc: True when the given location sits inside a designer-flagged no-search zone.

functions.name: ReportLocationBelief
GetLocationBeliefs
functions.doc: Every non-actor belief this AI currently holds, strongest first.

functions.name: GetStrongestLocationBelief
functions.doc: The strongest non-actor belief. False when the AI holds none.

functions.name: ClearLocationBelief
functions.doc: Drop a non-actor belief — the AI checked, there was nothing there.

functions.name: MakeActorSubject
functions.doc: A memory about a person, object or anything else with an actor.

functions.name: MakePlaceSubject
functions.doc:
A memory about a place. PlaceTag separates kinds of thing at one spot, so
 "a body here" and "a fight here" stay distinct memories.

functions.name: Remember
functions.doc:
Store something. Writing the same Tag about the same Subject again updates it
and increments Count, rather than piling up duplicates.

Every value field is optional — pass only what your game means by this tag.

functions.name: Recall
functions.doc: Everything held about a subject, newest first. False when nothing is.

functions.name: RecallTag
functions.doc: One specific memory. The usual query: "have I been attacked by this one?"

functions.name: HasMemoryOf
functions.doc: True if anything at all is held about this subject. Cheapest check.

functions.name: Forget
functions.doc: Drop one tag. Returns false if it was not there.

functions.name: ForgetSubject
functions.doc: Drop everything about a subject.

functions.name: ForgetEverything
functions.doc: Wipe the lot.

functions.name: GetRememberedSubjectCount
functions.doc: How many subjects are currently held. For budgeting and debugging.

functions.name: GetSenseBlocker
functions.doc:
Why a sense reported nothing about a target on its last evaluation.

Answers "why can't it see me" without guesswork: out of range, outside the
cone, occluded, not enough visible points, held by the reaction window.
Returns None when the sense did report something.

functions.name: ExplainPerception
functions.doc:
One line per sense saying what it did or why it did nothing. For logging
 and on-screen debugging.

functions.name: StartRecording
functions.doc:
Start recording this agent's belief, keeping the last Seconds of it.

Costs one small frame per tracked target per tick while running. Calling
this again restarts the window rather than extending it.

functions.name: StopRecording
functions.doc: Stop recording. What was captured stays available until cleared.

functions.name: GetRecordedFrames
functions.doc: Everything captured, oldest first.

functions.name: GetRecordedFramesFor
functions.doc: Just the frames about one target, oldest first.

functions.name: ClearRecording
functions.doc: Discard everything captured so far. Does not stop an active recording.

functions.name: GetRecordedFrameAt
functions.doc:
The recorded frame for Target nearest to World Seconds.

Returns false when nothing was recorded for that target. Use this to read
what the AI believed at the moment something went wrong, rather than what it
believes now that the moment has passed.

functions.name: ExplainRecordedAt
functions.doc:
Explain Perception, but for a moment already gone.

Reads the recorded frame nearest World Seconds and describes it the same way
the live trace does. Returns a note saying so when nothing was recorded.

functions.name: OnAISee
functions.doc: Vision sense confirmed a target. Fires while target is visible.

functions.name: OnAIHear
functions.doc: Hearing detected a sound. Fires once per sound event.

functions.name: OnAISmell
functions.doc: Smell sense detected a scent. Fires while scent is above threshold.

functions.name: OnAIFeel
functions.doc: Physical contact occurred (overlap, collision). Fires once per contact.

functions.name: OnAISenseVibration
functions.doc: Ground vibration detected — no line of sight required.

functions.name: OnAISuspect
functions.doc: First time confidence crosses SuspectThreshold. AI heard/smelled something.

functions.name: OnAIDetect
functions.doc: Confidence crossed DetectThreshold. Target confirmed.

functions.name: OnAITrack
functions.doc: Target is being actively tracked — high confidence, continuous perception.

functions.name: OnAILost
functions.doc: Lost perception of target. LastKnown, Predicted, and last cover object provided.

functions.name: OnAIRemember
functions.doc: Target is in Remembered state — stale belief, low confidence.

functions.name: OnAIForget
functions.doc: Target has fully expired from the ledger. AI has forgotten this target.

functions.name: OnAIThinkThreat
functions.doc: Threat level changed for a target. Fires on any change.

functions.name: OnAIAllClear
functions.doc: All active targets gone. Return to patrol.

functions.name: OnAIAwarenessChanged
functions.doc: Overall awareness level changed (Unaware / Peripheral / Suspicious / Alerted / Fully Aware).

functions.name: OnAIPainReported
functions.doc:
Fires when Report Pain From Definition is called.
PainType = the pain asset's name. PainLevel = current accumulated level 0-1.
ThresholdCrossed is always -1 (kept for compatibility). PainDef = the asset.

functions.name: OnAIDamaged
functions.doc:
Fires on every damage event received (ApplyDamage, ApplyRadialDamage, ApplyPointDamage).
Instigator is the Pawn behind the hit. Developer decides: call Report Pain,
Set Target Confidence, or ignore.

functions.name: OnAISquadAlert
functions.doc: A squadmate has shared target intel with this AI.

functions.name: OnAITelegraph
functions.doc:
Confidence about a target crossed Telegraph Threshold — the moment for a
 "huh?" bark or head-turn before the AI commits to full alert. Once per target.

functions.name: OnAttentionChanged
functions.doc: The AI's focus moved to a different target. Old Target is null on first acquisition.

functions.name: OnLocationBeliefChanged
functions.doc: A belief about a place — a noise with no author, a blast — changed state.

functions.name: GetOverriddenPropertyNames
functions.doc: Names of the fields this asset holds differently from its Parent Profile.

functions.name: ApplyArchetype
functions.doc: Stamp the chosen archetype's values onto this profile.

functions.name: ApplyArchetypeTo
functions.doc:
Set the fields an archetype defines, on any profile.

Exposed so a Blueprint can build a profile at runtime — spawn a profile,
apply Civilian, override two numbers, hand it to an agent.

functions.name: DescribeArchetype
functions.doc: One line describing what an archetype is for.

functions.name: EstimateBudget
functions.doc:
Rough per-second cost of running this profile, as text.

An estimate from the settings alone, not a measurement — it says what the
asset is asking for, which is the number worth knowing before a level is
full of agents rather than after.

functions.name: ShowBudget
functions.doc: Log the estimate for a level of 50 agents tracking 3 targets each.

functions.name: DiffAgainst
functions.doc: Every field where this profile differs from Other, as "Field: theirs -> mine".

functions.name: CompareWith
functions.doc: Log every field where this profile differs from Compare To.

functions.name: ShowComposition
functions.doc: Logs what is inherited and what is overridden, field by field.

functions.name: ValidateProfile
functions.doc:
Check this profile for settings that are contradictory, unreachable, or
simply inert — a weight keyed to a sense the profile does not run, a
threshold ordering that makes a state impossible to enter, a sample count
that another field silently overrides.

Findings are written to the Output Log. Run it from the Details panel after
editing a profile, or whenever an AI is behaving in a way the settings do
not seem to explain.

functions.name: EmitSound
EmitSoundAtLocation
GetAPSSubsystem
functions.doc:
Get the APS world subsystem from anywhere in Blueprint.

Drag off any node and search "Get APS Subsystem". Everything world-wide
lives here: ambient light, sun direction, weather, the perceivable-actor
registry and no-search zones.

functions.name: SetEnvironmentState
functions.doc: APS-P3: Full environment state setters

functions.name: SetSunDirection
functions.doc:
Tell APS which way the sun points so vision can trace for shadow and work
out whether a target is genuinely hidden in the dark. Pass your directional
light's forward vector.

functions.name: RegisterNeverSearchZone
functions.doc:
Register a sphere the AI will never search or pursue a target into.
Lets designers guarantee the player safe rooms — the guarantee Alien:
Isolation relied on and no engine system offers.

functions.name: UnregisterNeverSearchZone
functions.doc: Remove the closest registered zone within tolerance of Center.

functions.name: ClearNeverSearchZones
functions.doc: Clear every registered no-search zone.

functions.name: IsInNeverSearchZone
functions.doc: True when Location falls inside any registered no-search zone.

functions.name: RegisterPerceivableActor
functions.doc: Register an actor as perceivable. Call from BeginPlay on players/NPCs.

functions.name: UnregisterPerceivableActor
functions.doc: Unregister — call from EndPlay or when actor should no longer be perceived.

functions.name: SetPerceivedAsObject
functions.doc:
Mark an actor as a THING the AI perceives rather than someone: a body, a
forced lock, a dropped weapon. APS Evidence does this for its actor.

The AI still sees it, and its belief says how well (Get Belief Data, Get
Perceived Objects), but it is never a target: no threat, no attention, and no
event names it (On AI Suspect, On AI Detect, On AI See...). Takes effect on
each AI's next perception pass, so a guard that dies and becomes a body can
be marked then. This does not register it: pawns are found anyway, and any
other actor also needs Register Perceivable Actor.

functions.name: IsPerceivedAsObject
functions.doc: True while Actor is marked as a thing (Set Perceived As Object, APS Evidence).

functions.name: GetEnvironmentAt
functions.doc:
Conditions at a point, with any volumes covering it applied over the global
state. With no volumes registered this returns the global state unchanged,
so a project that never places one behaves exactly as it did before.

functions.name: GetSenseRangeScaleAt
GetAgentSignificance
functions.doc: Most recent significance score for an agent, [0..1]. Debug and tuning.

functions.name: EmitStimulus
functions.doc:
Emit a stimulus to all AI agents that can receive it.

Pipeline (cheapest checks first):
  1. Radius cull — agents beyond Event.Radius skipped
  2. LOD tier   — agents above Event.MaxLODTier skipped
  3. Team filter — agents on same team as Source skipped (if bTeamFilter)
  4. Wall trace  — occlusion check if Event.bRequiresClearPath
  5. Deliver to PerceptionCore::ReceiveStimulus()

All senses that registered a matching tag prefix receive the event.

Use this for any stimulus that should be centrally filtered and distributed.
Direct calls to ReportVibrationEvent / ReportSoundEvent bypass this pipeline.

functions.name: GetRelationship
functions.doc: Resolve relationship for a specific target actor.

functions.name: SetRelationshipOverride
functions.doc: Override relationship for a specific actor at runtime.

functions.name: Evaluate
functions.doc: Evaluate this sense against a single target.

functions.name: GetSenseID
functions.doc: Unique identifier. Return FName("Vision"), FName("MyRadar"), etc.

functions.name: ReportPainFromDefinition
functions.doc:
Report pain via DataAsset. Reads decay rate and sense effects from the asset.
Fires OnAIPainReported every call.

functions.name: GetPainLevelFromDefinition
functions.doc: Get current pain level by DataAsset. Returns 0 if unknown.

functions.name: GetTotalPainLevel
functions.doc: Get total combined pain across all active types (clamped 0-1).

functions.name: ClearPainFromDefinition
functions.doc: Remove pain using a DataAsset reference.

functions.name: ClearAllPain
functions.doc: Remove all pain of all types instantly.

functions.name: SetPainTypeEnabledFromDefinition
functions.display: Set Pain Type Enabled from Definition
functions.doc: Enable or disable a specific pain type by DataAsset.

functions.name: SetHealthRatio
functions.doc: Manually set health ratio for legacy health-based degradation.

functions.name: SetWindDirection
ReportContact
ReportContactWithImpulse
functions.doc: Report contact from a physics hit — maps impulse magnitude to strength automatically.

functions.name: EndTouchContact
functions.doc:
End a persistent contact (overlap ended).
Has no effect on one-shot contacts.

functions.name: ReportVibrationEvent
SetDescriptorTrait
functions.doc: Add a trait, or change its value if the key is already there.

functions.name: RemoveDescriptorTrait
functions.doc: Remove the trait with this key, if any.

functions.name: GetDescriptorTrait
functions.doc: The value held for a key. False when the descriptor says nothing about it.

functions.name: MatchAgainst
functions.doc:
How well Description fits Known, [0..1]. Only keys both hold are compared, and
each contradiction halves the score — the same rule Match Descriptor uses.

functions.name: SharedKeyCount
functions.doc:
How many keys the two have in common: a confident match on one trait is not
 a confident match on five.

functions.name: GetAge
functions.doc: Seconds this has existed. Read it to age a description — "still warm".

functions.name: RemoveEvidence
functions.doc: Remove it from the world. Hiding the body.

functions.name: ReportObservation
functions.doc:
Tell a faction something, arriving immediately and intact.

Merges into an existing entry when it plainly concerns the same subject —
either the same actor, or a description that matches one already on file —
so ten sightings of one suspect stay one manhunt.

@return the entry id, or -1 if nothing was recorded.

functions.name: ReportViaChannel
functions.doc:
The same, but sent along a channel — so it arrives late, vaguer, and missing
details, according to what that channel costs.

A radio report is not available the instant it is spoken. Until the delay
elapses the faction does not know, and anything that stops the sender in
that window stops the message.

functions.name: CancelPendingFrom
functions.doc:
Discard everything a sender has in flight but not yet delivered. Silencing
 the witness before the message lands.

functions.name: GetPendingCount
functions.doc: How many messages are still in transit.

functions.name: GetEntryForSubject
functions.doc: What the faction knows about a specific actor, if anything.

functions.name: GetEntries
functions.doc: Everything the faction currently believes, strongest first.

functions.name: MatchDescriptor
functions.doc:
Who fits this description?

The identity question, asked the way it is actually asked: not "where is
actor X" but "does anyone we know of look like this". Returns the best match
and how well it fits, so the caller decides whether that is enough to act on.

functions.name: ForgetEntry
functions.doc: Drop one entry — cleared, arrested, proven wrong.

functions.name: GetFactionAlert
functions.doc: How worked up a faction is, [0..1]. The generalised wanted level.

functions.name: GetObservationQuality
functions.doc:
How good a look this AI currently has at a target, [0..1].

Folds belief and distance into the single number that decides which traits
are made out. Exposed because it is worth being able to ask directly — "why
did my guard not notice the coat" has an answer here.

functions.name: ReportNow
functions.doc:
File a report now, ignoring the interval and confidence gates. For scripted
 moments — an alarm pull, a phone call.

functions.name: CancelMyPendingReports
functions.doc:
Everything this AI has personally filed and not yet had delivered. Cancel
 it and the report never arrives.

functions.name: GetProvenance
functions.doc: The provenance this observer stamps on its reports.

functions.name: OnEvidenceDiscovered
functions.doc:
Fires the first time this AI notices a given piece of evidence.

By the time it fires, a belief about the place and a memory have already been
recorded — so a handler can read them. What it MEANS is yours: raise the
alarm, investigate quietly, or step over it.

functions.name: GetDiscoveredEvidenceCount
functions.doc: Everything this AI has already found, so it does not rediscover it.

functions.name: BeginSearch
functions.doc: Begin searching from a last known position. Clears any search in progress.

functions.name: EndSearch
functions.doc: Stop, and release the grid.

functions.name: MarkCleared
functions.doc:
Mark somewhere as checked. Called automatically for wherever the owner
 goes; call it directly for a look down a corridor the AI did not enter.

functions.name: GetBestSearchPoint
functions.doc: The single best place to look next. False when nothing is left.

functions.name: GetRankedSearchPoints
functions.doc: The best N places, most promising first.

functions.name: IsSearchExhausted
functions.doc:
True once everything reachable has been checked — the AI has genuinely
 looked everywhere rather than merely run out of patience.

functions.name: GetSearchProgress
functions.doc:
Fraction of the reachable area already checked [0..1]. Drives "keep
 looking" versus "give up" without a hardcoded timer.

functions.name: GetSearchDuration
functions.doc: Seconds since the search began. What the reachable area is derived from.

functions.name: SetTrait
functions.doc: Set or replace one trait. The usual way to change a disguise at runtime.

functions.name: RemoveTrait
functions.doc: Remove a trait entirely — a dropped weapon, a discarded coat.

functions.name: GetObservedSubset
functions.doc:
The subset of this signature an observer would actually make out, given how
good the look was.

ObservationQuality folds together everything that affects a look: distance,
confidence, light. A trait is noticed when its Observability clears the
quality that was available — so a poor look yields only the obvious things,
and identity sharpens as the observer gets closer rather than arriving all
at once.

properties.name: Radius
properties.doc: Sphere of influence around the owning actor, in cm.

properties.name: Priority
properties.doc:
Higher wins where volumes overlap. Equal priorities resolve to whichever is
 nearer its own centre, so a small volume inside a large one takes effect.

properties.name: LightLevel
properties.doc: 0 is pitch dark, 1 is full daylight.

properties.name: bIsIndoors
properties.doc: Indoors concentrates scent and shelters from wind.

properties.name: VisionRangeScale
properties.doc: Smoke, fog, dust. 0.3 means vision reaches a third as far in here.

properties.name: HearingRangeScale
properties.doc:
A crowded market or a running generator. Below 1 makes it harder to hear
 anything specific; above 1 models a room that carries sound.

properties.name: Tag
properties.doc: What this is, in your vocabulary. "AttackedMe", "OwesMeMoney", "SeenWith".

properties.name: Number
properties.doc: A number, meaning whatever you decide. Damage taken, coins owed, a rating.

properties.name: Place
properties.doc: A place, if the memory has one. Where it happened, where they ran to.

properties.name: RelatedActor
properties.doc:
Another actor, if the memory links two things. This is what makes
 "seen with an accomplice" work without a special case for relationships.

properties.name: Count
properties.doc:
How many times this tag has been remembered about this subject.
 Maintained by APS because counting is bookkeeping, not meaning — you still
 decide whether three is a lot.

properties.name: Age
properties.doc: Seconds since this was last written.

properties.name: PlaceTag
properties.doc: What kind of place, when this is about a location rather than an actor.

properties.name: SenseID
properties.doc: "Vision", "Hearing", or whatever a custom sense returns from Get Sense ID.

properties.name: Confidence
properties.doc: What this sense reported, before weighting.

properties.name: Weight
properties.doc: The profile's weight for this sense.

properties.name: bIsActive
properties.doc: False when the sense is silent — it should contribute nothing.

properties.name: UpdateIntervalScale
properties.doc:
Multiplier on the profile's Base Update Interval. Above 1 means the whole
perception pass runs less often; below 1 makes it more responsive.

properties.name: SenseIntervalScale
properties.doc:
Multiplier on every per-sense evaluation interval. Lets vision be thinned
out independently of the core tick — useful when tracing is the cost and
the rest of the pipeline is not.

properties.name: MaxVisionSamples
properties.doc:
Hard cap on vision sample points per target, which is the single biggest
trace cost in the system. 0 leaves the profile's Vision Sample Count alone.

This only ever lowers the count — a quality asset cannot make an agent more
expensive than its profile asked for.

properties.name: bSkipPerTargetLight
properties.doc:
Skip per-target light sampling and the sun-shadow trace even when the
profile enables them, falling back to the global ambient level.

Worth knowing before enabling: this makes targets in shadow as visible as
targets in light, so it changes stealth behaviour, not just cost. Use it for
agents far enough away that nobody is judging their behaviour.

properties.name: VisibilitySamples
properties.default: { { TEXT("head"), FVector(0.f, 0.f, 85.f), 1.0f }, { NAME_None, FVector(0.f, 0.f, 50.f), 0.9f }, { NAME_None, FVector(0.f, 0.f, 0.f), 0.7f }, { TEXT("clavicle_l"), FVector(0.f, -30.f, 60.f), 0.6f }, { TEXT("clavicle_r"), FVector(0.f, 30.f, 60.f), 0.6f }, }
properties.doc:
Points the AI traces against to decide how exposed this actor is.
Socket names are resolved on the owner's skeletal mesh; entries with no
socket fall back to their local-space Offset.

Leave empty to inherit the observing AI's profile defaults.

properties.name: VisibilityMultiplier
properties.doc:
Flat multiplier on how visible this actor is [0..1].
Use for camouflage, ghillie suits, tall grass, or a cloaking device.
1 = normal, 0 = effectively invisible to sight.

properties.name: Stance
properties.doc: Current posture. Drives how many sample points must be visible to register.

properties.name: bAutoDetectStance
properties.doc: Read crouch state off the owning Character automatically each evaluation.

properties.name: LightLevelOverride
properties.doc:
Explicit light level at this actor [0..1]. -1 = let the AI work it out
from the sun-shadow trace. Drive this from your own light-gem system when
you want exact control over where the player is hidden.

properties.name: bAutoRegisterAsPerceivable
properties.doc: Register the owner as perceivable on BeginPlay so AI can find it with no extra setup.

properties.name: Apex
properties.doc: The fan's point: under the eyes on the floor, or at the eyes.

properties.name: Forward
properties.doc: Flat direction the fan's angles are measured from.

properties.name: Range
properties.doc: The cone's range before anything stops it (cm).

properties.name: FromDeg
properties.doc: The fan's edges, degrees about world up from Forward.

properties.name: ReachAhead
properties.doc: How far sight gets along the middle of the fan (cm): less than Range when something is in the way.

properties.name: Rim
properties.doc: Where sight ends, in order from FromDeg to ToDeg: world points at the Apex's height.

properties.name: RimAngles
properties.doc: Each rim point's angle from Forward (degrees).

properties.name: RimReach
properties.doc: How far sight gets to each rim point (cm).

properties.name: ConfidenceScale
properties.doc: How much a sighting in this cone counts: 1 for the focal cone, the profile's scale for the others.

properties.name: Transmission
properties.doc: How much of vision reaches it, 0 (blocked) to 1 (clear).

properties.name: Weight
properties.doc: The point's weight in the exposure: how much of the target it stands for.

properties.name: Origin
properties.doc: Where the sound was made.

properties.name: Source
properties.doc: Who made it. None for a noise with no maker (Emit Sound At Location).

properties.name: SoundName
properties.doc: The Sound Type's name, e.g. "Creak". "Sound" when it has none.

properties.name: DisplayName
properties.doc: Sound Name as words, for a label: "FootstepWalk" reads "Footstep Walk".

properties.name: Loudness
properties.doc: How loud it was made (the Sound Type's loudness times the emitter's multiplier).

properties.name: Heard
properties.doc: How loud it reached this AI, 0 to 1: after distance, walls and rain. What hearing works with.

properties.name: Reach
properties.doc: How far this sound carries to this AI (cm): the Sound Type's range, scaled where the AI stands.

properties.name: Distance
properties.doc: From the sound to this AI (cm).

properties.name: Walls
properties.doc: Walls between the sound and this AI's ear. 0 when the path is clear.

properties.name: bNoMaker
properties.doc: A noise with no maker: it becomes a belief about the place, not about anyone.

properties.name: Time
properties.doc: World seconds when it was heard.

properties.name: VisionHalfAngle
properties.doc: Half the focal cone's width (degrees).

properties.name: Peripheral
properties.doc: 0 when the peripheral cone is off.

properties.name: RearMotion
properties.doc: 0 when the rear-motion cone is off.

properties.name: Hearing
properties.doc: Hearing's cap, scaled by any quiet or loud zone the AI stands in. A Sound Type can carry less far (Get Sound Reach).

properties.name: bEchoDirectional
properties.doc: Echolocation pings forward only, about 101 degrees to each side.

properties.name: DominantEmotion
properties.doc: Dominant emotion this tick (highest value above threshold).

properties.name: FearInput
properties.doc: External fear input [0..1]. Set via SetFearInput(). Drives Fear rise when > 0.

properties.name: SenseClass
properties.doc: Sense to impair. Select from the dropdown — e.g. Vision Sense, Hearing Sense.

properties.name: Effect
properties.doc: Impairment strength [0-1]. At PainLevel=1 and Effect=1 the sense is at its floor.

properties.name: DisplayName
properties.doc: A readable name for this pain type, for your own UI.

properties.name: DebugColor
properties.doc: A colour for this pain type, for your own UI or debug view.

properties.name: DecayRate
properties.doc:
How fast pain level decays per second when not refreshed.
0.05 = very slow (bleeding lingers)
0.2  = moderate (burning fades)
1.0  = fast (stun wears off quickly)
0.0  = never decays (requires manual ClearPain call)

properties.name: MaxLevel
properties.doc:
Maximum pain level this type can reach [0-1].
1.0 = can reach full impairment.
0.5 = caps at 50% regardless of how many times ReportPain is called.

properties.name: AmountOverride
properties.doc:
How much each ReportPain call adds to the pain level.
If 0, the raw PainAmount passed to ReportPain is used directly.
If > 0, this overrides the caller's amount (useful for binary pain types).

properties.name: ProfileOverrides
properties.doc:
Changes applied to this one agent's copy of the profile.

Leave empty and the agent shares the profile asset directly, which costs
nothing. Add an entry and this agent gets a private resolved copy.

properties.name: QualityProfile
properties.doc:
Optional cost controls applied on top of the profile. Leave empty for full
quality. Changing this never resets what the AI believes — that is the whole
reason it is separate from the profile.

properties.name: bShowVisualizer
properties.doc:
Show this AI with the APS Visualizer. Its actor is spawned at Begin Play and
removed with the AI. Off: nothing is shown and nothing is spent on it.

properties.name: VisualizerClass
properties.doc:
The Visualizer to spawn: the plugin's BP_APSVisualizer by default. Make a child
Blueprint of it to restyle it, or any actor of your own that reads the View nodes.

properties.name: bRecordHeardSounds
properties.doc:
Keep the sounds this AI hears for Get Recent Sounds. On by itself while a
Visualizer is shown or On Sound Heard is bound; working out how loud each sound
arrived costs a few traces per sound, so it is otherwise skipped.

properties.name: bPausePerception
properties.doc:
Stop every sense: nothing new is perceived while paused, and beliefs fade as they would with nothing in
 view. For watching memory and decay on their own.

properties.name: OnAISee
properties.doc: Vision is seeing a target. Fires every perception tick while it is visible.

properties.name: OnAIHear
properties.doc: Hearing picked up a sound from a target.

properties.name: OnAISmell
properties.doc: Smell is picking up a target's scent.

properties.name: OnAIFeel
properties.doc: Something touched the AI — a bump, a grab, a collision.

properties.name: OnAISenseVibration
properties.doc: Ground vibration was felt. Needs no line of sight.

properties.name: OnAISuspect
properties.doc: A target became Suspected: the AI noticed something but is not sure yet.

properties.name: OnAIDetect
properties.doc: A target became Detected: the AI is sure it is there.

properties.name: OnAITrack
properties.doc: A target became Tracked: high, sustained confidence.

properties.name: OnAILost
properties.doc: A target was Lost. Gives the last known and predicted positions, and the cover it was last near.

properties.name: OnAIRemember
properties.doc: A lost target faded to Remembered: the AI still knows it was there.

properties.name: OnAIForget
properties.doc: The AI let go of a target entirely (Expired, or back to Undetected).

properties.name: OnAIThinkThreat
properties.doc: Fires on any threat level change.

properties.name: OnThreatIdentified
properties.doc: Fires only when threat reaches High or Critical.

properties.name: OnAIAllClear
properties.doc: All active targets gone — return to patrol.

properties.name: OnAIAwarenessChanged
properties.doc: The AI's overall alert level changed (Unaware, Peripheral, Suspicious, Alerted, Fully Aware).

properties.name: OnAIPainReported
properties.doc:
Fires when ReportPainFromDefinition() is called on the Pain sense.
PainDef  = the DataAsset that describes this pain type.
PainLevel = current accumulated level 0-1.

properties.name: OnAIDamaged
properties.doc:
Fires on every damage event the AI owner receives.
Catches ApplyDamage, ApplyRadialDamage, ApplyPointDamage automatically.
Developer decides what to do: call ReportPain, SetTargetConfidence, or ignore.

properties.name: OnTargetStateChanged
properties.doc: Fires on every lifecycle state change — provides old and new state.

properties.name: OnEmotionalStateChanged
properties.doc: Fires when dominant emotion changes.

properties.name: OnAttentionChanged
properties.doc:
Fires when the AI's attention shifts to a different primary target.
OldTarget = previous focus (may be null on first acquisition).
NewTarget = new focus target.
Use in BT to cancel current pursuit and re-plan.

properties.name: OnAISquadAlert
properties.doc: A squadmate shared intel or raised an alert about a target.

properties.name: OnCombatRoleAssigned
properties.doc: Fires when this AI is assigned a combat role.

properties.name: OnSoundHeard
properties.doc:
Fires for every sound this AI hears, after its sound filter: where it came from, how
loud it was made and how loud it arrived, the distance, the walls between and whether
the path was clear. A noise with no maker is included (No Maker). Once per sound per
perception pass.

properties.name: ReplicatedTargets
properties.doc:
Compact per-target perception summary, replicated to clients when the
profile enables it. Perception stays server-authoritative — this exists so
detection meters, HUD and spectator tools work on clients without every
project hand-rolling its own replication.

properties.name: ReplicatedAwareness
properties.doc: Highest awareness level across all targets. Replicated.

properties.name: OnReplicatedStateChanged
properties.doc: Fires on clients whenever the replicated perception summary changes.

properties.name: OnAITelegraph
properties.doc:
Fires once per target when confidence crosses TelegraphThreshold — before
the AI commits to full alert. Hook a "huh?" bark or head-turn here so the
player can read that they are about to be spotted.

properties.name: OnLocationBeliefChanged
properties.doc: Fires when a non-actor belief changes lifecycle state.

properties.name: SourceProfile
properties.doc:
The asset as assigned, kept so composition can be redone when an override
 changes. Null when the profile needed no composition and Profile is the
 shared asset itself.

properties.name: RecordedFrames
properties.doc: Rolling capture. Bounded by Recording Window Seconds, oldest dropped first.

properties.name: FusionPolicyInst
properties.doc:
Instantiated from the profile when it names a class, null otherwise. Null is
the common case and means "run the built-in path", so an unconfigured
project pays nothing for these existing.

properties.name: CachedListener
properties.doc:
Cached PawnSensing-style listener on the owning actor (optional).
 Resolved once in BeginPlay. When present, PerceptionCore forwards every
 sense/lifecycle/brain/squad broadcast to its matching BlueprintNativeEvent
 so designers can override events directly without binding delegates.

properties.name: CachedTargetList
properties.doc:
Candidates from the last gather. A UPROPERTY so garbage collection sees it:
 it outlives a frame (refreshed every few ticks, or far less often for a
 throttled agent), and a raw pointer to an actor destroyed in between was a
 dangling pointer once GC ran — the reference is now cleared instead.

properties.name: ParentProfile
properties.doc:
Inherit every setting from this profile, keeping only the fields changed here.

A field counts as changed when it differs from the class default — exactly
the fields the Details panel marks with a revert-to-default arrow. Leave a
field alone and it tracks the parent; edit it and it is yours.

Start a child from a NEW profile rather than a duplicate of the parent. A
duplicate carries every one of the parent's tuned values as changed fields,
so it would inherit nothing and drift the moment the parent moves on.

To pin a value that happens to equal the class default, put it in Overrides
below — that list is read after inheritance and always wins.

Composition is resolved once, when an agent starts or swaps profiles, into
a private copy owned by that agent. Editing the parent therefore affects
agents that spawn afterwards, not ones already running.

Use Show Composition to see exactly which fields are inherited.

properties.name: Overrides
properties.doc:
Extra changes stamped on after inheritance is resolved.

Rarely needed on an asset — editing the field directly is the normal way to
override one. This exists for values a Blueprint wants to compute, and it is
the same list the component uses for per-agent tweaks.

properties.name: Archetype
properties.doc:
Preset to stamp onto this profile when Apply Archetype is pressed.

Applying overwrites the fields the archetype cares about and leaves the rest
alone. It is a starting point, not a mode — nothing reads this at runtime.

properties.name: CompareTo
properties.doc: The profile Compare With reports differences against.

properties.name: SenseClasses
properties.doc:
Sense classes to instantiate on this AI. Order = slot index.

A new profile starts with Vision and Hearing already here, so an AI works
the moment you assign the profile. Add Smell, Touch, Vibration, Damage,
Pain or Echolocation as you need them — or remove Hearing for an AI that
only sees. An empty list means the AI perceives nothing at all.

properties.name: FusionPolicy
properties.doc: How several senses combine into one confidence value.

properties.name: ThreatPolicy
properties.doc:
How dangerous a target is. The level is still derived from the Brain|Threat
 thresholds below, so a policy only supplies the score.

properties.name: AttentionPolicy
properties.doc: Which target the AI commits its focus to.

properties.name: SenseWeights
properties.doc: Per-sense confidence weight. Missing = 1.0.

properties.name: SenseIntervals
properties.doc: Per-sense tick interval override (seconds). Missing = sense default.

properties.name: VisionMaxRange
properties.doc: Vision: max sight distance (cm).

properties.name: HearingMaxRange
properties.doc: Hearing: max sound detection range (cm). Individual sound assets define per-type ranges.

properties.name: SmellMaxRange
properties.doc: Smell: max scent detection range (cm).

properties.name: VibrationDetectRange
properties.doc: Vibration: max ground vibration range (cm). Passes through walls.

properties.name: EchoRange
properties.doc: Echolocation: sonar pulse range (cm).

properties.name: bAutoConfidenceFromDamage
properties.doc:
If true, damage automatically builds target confidence (default behavior).
 If false, damage fires OnAIDamaged delegate only — developer calls SetTargetConfidence themselves.

properties.name: VisionHalfAngleDeg
properties.doc: Vision cone half-angle (degrees). 60 = standard forward cone.

properties.name: VisionSampleCount
properties.doc: Ray sample count per target (1-5). More = better partial cover detection, higher cost.

properties.name: DarknessMinDetection
properties.doc: Minimum detection in total darkness [0..1]. 0 = fully blind in dark.

properties.name: EyeHeightOffset
properties.doc:
Eye height offset from actor root (cm). Used when bUseEyeSocket is false,
 or as a fallback when the configured socket does not exist.

properties.name: bUseEyeSocket
properties.doc:
Take the eye position from a mesh socket instead of the fixed EyeHeightOffset.
 The cone origin then follows head animation every frame.

properties.name: EyeSocketName
properties.doc: Socket / bone the eyes sit on. Typical: "head", "eyes", "S_Eyes".

properties.name: EyeDirectionMode
properties.doc: Where the cone's FACING comes from. Socket Rotation makes the cone follow the head bone.

properties.name: EyeSocketAlignment
properties.doc:
How the socket's rotation becomes a look direction.
