Leave on Automatic and you can point EyeSocketName straight at a bone —
"head", "eyes", whatever your rig calls it — with no other setup. APS reads
the skeleton's reference pose, works out how that bone is oriented relative
to the character, and cancels it. The cone then starts along the character's
forward and follows the bone as it animates.

properties.name: EyeSocketRotationOffset
properties.doc:
Hand-authored correction, used only when EyeSocketAlignment is Manual Offset.
Rotates the socket's forward onto the character's forward.

properties.name: EyeSocketRotationWeight
properties.doc:
Blended mode only: how much of the facing comes from the socket [0..1].
 0 = pure actor rotation, 1 = pure socket rotation.

properties.name: EyeTurnRateDegPerSec
properties.doc:
Degrees per second the perception facing may turn. 0 = instant (Epic's behaviour,
 where the cone snaps to a MoveTo target before the body has turned).
 Set this near your mesh's actual turn rate so the AI cannot see you before
 it has physically turned to look.
properties.display: Eye Turn Rate Deg Per Sec

properties.name: DefaultVisibilitySamples
properties.doc:
Sample points traced when the target has no APS Target Component.
 Offsets are in the target's LOCAL space, so they rotate with it — a prone
 or turned target samples the right places. Leave empty to use the built-in
 head / chest / pelvis / shoulders set.

properties.name: MinExposureToRegister
properties.doc:
Minimum weighted exposure [0..1] before the target counts as seen at all.
 0 = any single visible point registers. Raise it so a sliver of shoulder
 behind cover is not a full detection.

properties.name: MinVisiblePoints_Standing
properties.doc:
Minimum number of visible sample points required before a target registers,
per stance. Splinter Cell's rule: a crouched target behind cover should need
more of itself exposed than a standing one before the AI commits.

All three default to 1, meaning stance changes nothing until you opt in —
adding an APS Target Component must never silently make a character harder
to see. Raise Crouched to 2 and Prone to 3 for the stance-aware behaviour.

properties.name: VisionOcclusionChannels
properties.doc:
Collision channels tested when checking line of sight. Epic tests one channel,
 which is why AI routinely sees through doors, vehicles and other pawns.
 Empty = Visibility only.

properties.name: bPawnsBlockSight
properties.doc: If true, other perceivable actors block line of sight (bodies are occluders).

properties.name: SurfaceVisionTransmission
properties.doc:
Per-surface vision dampening. Value = fraction of vision that PASSES THROUGH
 that surface [0..1]. 1 = fully transparent (glass), 0 = fully solid (concrete),
 0.4 = partial (foliage, smoke). Surfaces not listed block completely.

properties.name: bUseSeparateVerticalFOV
properties.doc:
Use a separate vertical half-angle, making the cone elliptical instead of
 perfectly round. Essential for games with verticality.

properties.name: VisionVerticalHalfAngleDeg
properties.doc: Vertical (pitch) half-angle in degrees. Only used when bUseSeparateVerticalFOV.

properties.name: bEnablePeripheralCone
properties.doc: Enable a wider, weaker peripheral cone outside the focal cone.

properties.name: PeripheralHalfAngleDeg
properties.doc: Peripheral half-angle (degrees). Should exceed VisionHalfAngleDeg.

properties.name: PeripheralConfidenceScale
properties.doc: Confidence multiplier for detections made in the peripheral cone.

properties.name: PeripheralRangeScale
properties.doc: Fraction of VisionMaxRange the peripheral cone reaches.

properties.name: bEnableRearMotionCone
properties.doc:
Enable a rear cone that only registers MOVING targets — Thief's "false vision"
 cone. Stops players walking straight up behind an AI with impunity, without
 making the AI omniscient.

properties.name: RearMotionHalfAngleDeg
properties.doc: Rear cone half-angle measured from directly BEHIND the AI (degrees).

properties.name: RearMotionMinSpeed
properties.doc: Target must move at least this fast (cm/s) to register in the rear cone.

properties.name: RearMotionConfidenceScale
properties.doc: Confidence multiplier for rear-cone detections. Keep low — this is a hint, not sight.

properties.name: RearMotionRangeScale
properties.doc: Fraction of VisionMaxRange the rear cone reaches.

properties.name: bUsePerTargetLight
properties.doc:
Sample light AT THE TARGET rather than using one global ambient value.
 Without this, a dark corner is indistinguishable from broad daylight —
 the global level only models day/night.

properties.name: bTraceSunShadow
properties.doc:
Trace from the target toward the sun to decide whether it is in shadow.
 Set the sun on the APS subsystem with SetSunDirection().

properties.name: ShadowLightLevel
properties.doc: Light level applied when the target is in shadow [0..1].

properties.name: SunTraceDistance
properties.doc: How far the shadow trace reaches (cm).

properties.name: VisionDistanceCurve
properties.doc: Curve: X = normalized distance [0..1], Y = confidence multiplier.

properties.name: VisionAngleCurve
properties.doc: Curve: X = normalized angle [0..1], Y = confidence multiplier.

properties.name: MotionBonusCurve
properties.doc: Curve: X = target speed (cm/s), Y = detectability multiplier [0.5..1.5].

properties.name: bKeyholeVision
properties.doc: Enable keyhole-shaped vision cone.

properties.name: KeyholeNearAngle
properties.doc: Half-angle at close range (≤ KeyholeNearDistance).

properties.name: KeyholeFarAngle
properties.doc: Half-angle at maximum range.

properties.name: KeyholeNearDistance
properties.doc: Distance at which KeyholeNearAngle is fully applied (cm).

properties.name: HearingBaseThreshold
properties.doc: Base noise threshold. Lower = more sensitive.

properties.name: WallAbsorptionCoeff
properties.doc: Wall absorption per wall hit. Higher = more muffled.

properties.name: bSoundEventOnlyMode
properties.doc: If true, only explicit EmitSound() calls trigger hearing.

properties.name: SoundFilter
properties.doc: Optional sound filter — which categories/alert levels this AI hears.

properties.name: SoundAccumulationRate
properties.doc: Confidence build rate per second from repeated sounds.

properties.name: SoundAccumulationHoldTime
properties.doc: Seconds of silence before accumulated sound confidence starts decaying.

properties.name: SoundAccumulationDecayRate
properties.doc: Confidence decay rate per second after hold time expires.

properties.name: SmellAccumulationRate
properties.doc: How fast smell confidence builds per second while in range.

properties.name: SmellDecayRate
properties.doc: How fast smell confidence decays per second after target leaves range.

properties.name: VibrationMinSpeed
properties.doc: Minimum target movement speed (cm/s) to produce detectable vibration.

properties.name: TouchConfidence
properties.doc: Confidence assigned on physical contact. 1.0 = instant full detection.

properties.name: TouchMaxImpulseForFullStrength
properties.doc: Physics impulse magnitude that maps to Strength=1.0.
properties.display: Touch Max Impulse for Full Strength

properties.name: TouchPersistentAccumulationRate
properties.doc: Confidence gained per second while a persistent contact is held.

properties.name: TouchMaxPersistentBonus
properties.doc: Maximum extra confidence from persistent contact duration.

properties.name: bEchoDirectional
properties.doc: If true, only detects targets in the front hemisphere.

properties.name: VisionLoss
properties.doc: Vision loss — hide behind wall → how fast AI loses you. Default: 0.3s, direct cut.

properties.name: HearingLoss
properties.doc: Hearing loss — sounds stop → how fast AI forgets. Default: 3.0s, step-down.

properties.name: SmellLoss
properties.doc: Smell loss — target leaves range → scent lingers. Default: 20.0s, step-down.

properties.name: TouchLoss
properties.doc: Touch loss — contact ends → how fast AI loses target. Default: 0.5s, step-down.

properties.name: VibrationLoss
properties.doc: Vibration loss — movement stops → instant loss. Default: 0.0s.

properties.name: DamageLoss
properties.doc: Damage loss — AI remembers being hit for a long time. Default: 8.0s.

properties.name: EcholocationLoss
properties.doc: Echolocation loss — sonar pulse missed. Default: 0.6s, direct cut.

properties.name: CorroborationBonus
properties.doc:
Flat confidence bonus added per extra active sense beyond the first.
Example: Vision=0.8 alone → 0.8. Vision + Hearing both active → 0.8 + 0.1 = 0.9.
Keep low (0.05-0.15). 0 = best-sense-only, no corroboration.

properties.name: ConfidenceRiseRate
properties.doc: How fast confidence rises when a sense is active. Higher = snappier detection.

properties.name: ConfidenceDecaySmoothing
properties.doc: How fast confidence falls while senses are still active but weakening.

properties.name: StandingDwellRate
properties.doc: Confidence climb rate per second for a stationary target.

properties.name: MovingDwellRate
properties.doc: Confidence climb rate per second for a sprinting target.

properties.name: ConfidenceReduceDelay
properties.doc: Seconds before confidence starts reducing after target weakens.

properties.name: DecayCurve
properties.doc: Curve: X = seconds since last sensed, Y = decay multiplier. Leave null = exponential.

properties.name: LongTermDecayCurve
properties.doc: Curve for long-term memory. Much slower decay than primary.

properties.name: DefaultDecayExponent
properties.doc: Fallback exponential decay rate when no DecayCurve set. Higher = forgets faster.

properties.name: MemoryRefreshBonus
properties.doc: Confidence bonus when re-detecting a previously lost target.

properties.name: MemoryExpireThreshold
properties.doc: Confidence below which a Remembered target becomes Expired and removed.

properties.name: MinTimeInLost
properties.doc:
Minimum seconds the AI must spend in Lost before it can transition to Remembered.
 0 = no delay (default). Increase to make the AI search longer before giving up.

properties.name: SuspectThreshold
properties.doc: Confidence to enter Suspected state.

properties.name: DetectThreshold
properties.doc: Confidence to enter Detected state.

properties.name: TrackThreshold
properties.doc: Confidence to enter Tracked state.

properties.name: FullAwareThreshold
properties.doc: Confidence for FullyAware awareness level (used by OnAIAwarenessChanged).

properties.name: MinTrackDuration
properties.doc: Minimum seconds in Detected before transitioning to Tracked. Prevents instant lock.

properties.name: AttentionStickinessTime
properties.doc:
Minimum seconds AI stays focused on current target before switching.
Guard=2s, Zombie=5s, Robot=0.5s, Animal=3s, Boss=1s.

properties.name: AttentionSwitchThreshold
properties.doc: New target's score must exceed current by this much before AI switches focus.

properties.name: bEnableSpatialModel
properties.doc: Enable spatial belief model (LastKnownPosition, PredictedPosition, UncertaintyRadius).

properties.name: bEnablePrediction
properties.doc: Enable predictive position extrapolation when target is Lost.

properties.name: PredictionHorizon
properties.doc: Seconds ahead to project target position when Lost.

properties.name: MaxPredictionTime
properties.doc: Maximum time horizon for prediction (seconds).

properties.name: UncertaintyGrowthRate
properties.doc: Rate at which uncertainty radius expands after losing target (cm/s).

properties.name: MaxUncertaintyRadius
properties.doc: Maximum uncertainty radius (cm).

properties.name: bVelocityScaledUncertainty
properties.doc: If true, fast-moving targets produce larger uncertainty when lost.

properties.name: VelocityEMAWeight
properties.doc: EMA weight for velocity smoothing [0-1]. Lower = smoother, higher = more reactive.

properties.name: bAsyncVisionTraces
properties.doc:
Issue vision's visibility traces asynchronously, reading the results on the
next evaluation instead of blocking on them.

Vision is the single largest trace cost in the system, and this moves it off
the game thread. The trade is that exposure describes where the target was
one evaluation ago — about 0.15 s at default settings — so a target crossing
cover quickly is judged a fraction late.

Off by default: it is a performance choice with a behavioural cost, and that
is the project's call rather than a default anyone should inherit. Per-surface
transmission always stays synchronous, since partial results across frames
cannot express it correctly.

properties.name: bEnableStatisticalTier
properties.doc:
Let very distant agents perceive statistically instead of geometrically.

Above the tier below, an agent stops tracing entirely. Detection becomes a
probability rolled against distance, light and movement — no line of sight,
no sample points, no cone sweep. It costs a few multiplies per candidate
instead of a dozen traces, which is what makes a crowd of civilians into
plausible witnesses rather than scenery.

They are NOT blind and they are NOT accurate. An agent in this tier will
occasionally notice someone it has no line of sight to, and occasionally
miss someone standing in front of it. That is the trade, and it only holds
up at a distance where nobody is watching closely enough to tell.

Off by default: geometric perception is what this plugin is for, and an
approximation should never be something a project inherits by accident.

properties.name: StatisticalTierThreshold
properties.doc:
LOD tier at or above which statistical perception replaces the real thing.
 3 is roughly 15 km from the nearest viewer at default significance.

properties.name: StatisticalDetectionRate
properties.doc:
Chance per second of noticing an ideally-placed target — close, lit, moving.
 Everything else scales this down.

properties.name: StatisticalDetectionConfidence
properties.doc:
Confidence granted when a statistical detection lands. Deliberately modest:
 a distant agent that half-noticed something should be suspicious, not certain.

properties.name: BaseUpdateInterval
properties.doc: Base perception tick interval (seconds). Lower = more reactive, higher CPU cost.

properties.name: MaintenanceInterval
properties.doc: How often the ledger runs maintenance — expire old records, compact (seconds).

properties.name: MaxTrackedTargets
properties.doc: Maximum number of targets tracked simultaneously.

properties.name: bDistanceTickThrottling
properties.doc:
Stop dispatching a tick every frame for agents that are very far from the
camera (LOD tier 3 and 4 — beyond 15 km).

Without this the component still receives a full tick every frame at those
distances purely to accumulate time and return early. The perception rate
itself does not change: the accumulator is fed the real elapsed time either
way, so decay and lifecycle timing are identical. Tiers 0-2 are untouched,
which is what keeps debug drawing smooth on any agent you can actually see.

Turn off if you drive LOD tiers yourself and want every agent ticking at
frame rate regardless of distance.

properties.name: SortWeightConfidence
properties.doc: Sort score weight: confidence.

properties.name: SortWeightRecency
properties.doc: Sort score weight: recency.

properties.name: SortWeightProximity
properties.doc: Sort score weight: proximity.

properties.name: MaxSortDistance
properties.doc: Max distance considered for sort scoring (cm).

properties.name: MaxFear
properties.doc: Max fear level [0..1]. Set to 0 to disable fear entirely.

properties.name: EmotionActiveThreshold
properties.doc: Minimum value for an emotion to be considered active (affects DominantEmotion).

properties.name: PanicOverrideThreshold
properties.doc: Panic overrides all other emotions above this value.

properties.name: ThreatDamageDecayRate
properties.doc: Rate damage contribution decays per second when target is not sensed. 0 = never decays.

properties.name: SquadShareRange
properties.doc: Max range to share intel with squadmates (cm).

properties.name: MinThreatToShare
properties.doc: Minimum threat level before this AI shares target with squad.

properties.name: bAutoShareOnDetect
properties.doc: Auto-share on Detected — true = horde/pack. False = tactical (manual only).

properties.name: bAutoShareOnTrack
properties.doc: Auto-share on Tracked (only if bAutoShareOnDetect=false, prevents double-sharing).

properties.name: EligibleRoles
properties.doc: Combat roles this archetype is eligible for. Empty = any role.

properties.name: bEnablePlayerBehaviorModel
properties.doc: Enable per-session player behavior observation and adaptation.

properties.name: MinEngagementsRequired
properties.doc: Minimum engagements before AI adapts. Prevents premature adaptation.

properties.name: PlayerCrouchSpeedThreshold
properties.doc: Speed below which player is considered crouching (cm/s).

properties.name: PlayerSprintSpeedThreshold
properties.doc: Speed above which player is considered sprinting (cm/s).

properties.name: MemoryMaxSubjects
properties.doc:
Distinct subjects one agent may hold memories about. The least recently
 written is dropped when this is exceeded.

properties.name: MemoryMaxTagsPerSubject
properties.doc: Distinct tags per subject. The oldest is dropped when this is exceeded.

properties.name: MemoryRetentionSeconds
properties.doc:
Seconds a memory survives without being written again. 0 = the whole
 session. Defaulted to a real value rather than 0, so an agent that meets a
 great many things releases them without anyone having to think about it.

properties.name: PainVisionFloor
properties.doc: Vision floor at 0% HP — sense degradation will not go below this value.

properties.name: bAutoWireTouchEvents
properties.doc:
Automatically route the owner's collision hits and overlaps into the Touch
 sense. Without this every bump has to be hand-wired from Blueprint.

properties.name: bAutoWireOverlapAsGrab
properties.doc: Treat overlaps (not just blocking hits) as persistent contact.

properties.name: FirstSpotReactionTime
properties.doc:
Seconds the AI must hold a target before confidence begins accumulating,
 on FIRST acquisition only. This is reaction time: it gives the player a
 beat to break line of sight after stepping into view. 0 = instant.

properties.name: TelegraphThreshold
properties.doc:
Confidence at which OnAITelegraph fires — a hook to play a "huh?" bark or
 head-turn BEFORE the AI commits to full alert, so detection is readable.
 Should sit between SuspectThreshold and DetectThreshold.

properties.name: bOffscreenHearingPenalty
properties.doc:
Reduce hearing sensitivity while this AI is off every player's screen.
 Stops unseen AI reacting to noise the player never saw them hear.

properties.name: OffscreenHearingMultiplier
properties.doc: Hearing multiplier applied while off-screen [0..1].

properties.name: bRespectNeverSearchZones
properties.doc:
Honour designer-flagged no-search zones registered on the APS subsystem.
 A target whose last known position falls inside one is never pursued there,
 guaranteeing the player safe rooms.

properties.name: bReplicatePerceptionState
properties.doc:
Replicate a compact per-target perception summary to clients so client-side
 detection meters, HUD and spectator tools work without custom plumbing.
 Perception itself stays server-authoritative.

properties.name: MaxReplicatedTargets
properties.doc:
Maximum targets included in the replicated summary. Keep small — this is
 bandwidth on every AI.

properties.name: ReplicationInterval
properties.doc: Seconds between replicated state refreshes.

properties.name: bUseReplicationRelevance
properties.doc:
Only publish targets a viewer could plausibly care about.

Without this every AI publishes its whole shortlist to every client, and the
bandwidth scales with agents times targets whether or not anyone can see the
outcome. Relevance is judged against the nearest local viewer, so a guard
tracking someone on the far side of the map stops paying for it.

properties.name: ReplicationRelevanceRange
properties.doc:
Beyond this from every viewer, a target is dropped from the summary (cm).
 0 disables the distance test and keeps only the confidence one.

properties.name: ReplicationMinConfidence
properties.doc:
Below this confidence a target is not worth the bandwidth. A detection meter
 that has barely flickered is not something a client needs told about.

properties.name: bSkipUnchangedReplication
properties.doc:
Skip the update entirely when nothing meaningfully changed.

The summary is rebuilt on a timer regardless of whether belief moved, and
writing an identical array still dirties the property and sends it. This
compares against what was last published and stays quiet when the difference
is below the threshold below.

properties.name: ReplicationConfidenceDelta
properties.doc: How much confidence must move before it is worth sending.

properties.name: SignificancePolicy
properties.doc:
How importance is scored. Leave empty for the built-in rule, which weighs
distance to the nearest viewer against whether the agent is engaged.

properties.name: MaxPerceptionUpdatesPerFrame
properties.doc:
Most agents allowed a full perception pass in one frame. 0 is unlimited,
which is the default and matches every build before this existed.

Above zero, only that many agents run a full pass per frame. Slots go to
agents whose pass is due, ranked by how long they have waited weighted by
significance, so a less significant agent is delayed but never starved. A
deferred agent drops nothing: its accumulated time still arrives, so decay
and lifecycle timing stay correct — it simply arrives in one larger step.

properties.name: Property
properties.doc: Exact name of the profile property to change, e.g. "VisionMaxRange".

properties.name: Number
properties.doc: Value for numeric properties - float, int32, byte and enum.

properties.name: bFlag
properties.doc: Value for bool properties. Ignored when the named property is numeric.

properties.name: Tag
properties.doc: What kind of thing was observed — "Sound.Gunshot", "Evidence.Body".

properties.name: LocationAccuracy
properties.doc: How precisely the position is known [0..1]. Drives uncertainty radius.

properties.name: SocketName
properties.doc: Mesh socket / bone to trace against. None = use Offset instead.

properties.name: Offset
properties.doc:
Local-space fallback offset from the actor root (cm), used when SocketName is None
 or the socket does not exist. Rotated by the target's facing, unlike a raw world offset.

properties.name: Weight
properties.doc: Relative importance of this point [0..1]. A visible head counts for more than a visible foot.

properties.name: HowLost
properties.doc: How this engagement ended.

properties.name: StateWhenLost
properties.doc: State before going Lost (was AI Tracked or just Detected?).

properties.name: LocationWhenLost
properties.doc: World position of target when AI lost them.

properties.name: AICameraDirection
properties.doc: Direction AI was facing when they lost the target. Useful for predicting blind spots.

properties.name: TargetFleeDireciton
properties.doc: Direction target was moving when lost (from EstimatedVelocity).

properties.name: EngagementDuration
properties.doc: How long this engagement lasted in seconds (from first Detected to Lost).

properties.name: PeakThreatLevel
properties.doc: Peak threat level reached during this engagement.

properties.name: WorldTimeStamp
properties.doc: World time when this episode was recorded. Use for "was this recent?" checks.

properties.name: ExposureRatio
properties.doc:
Weighted fraction of visibility sample points with a clear line to the observer [0..1].
 Vision only. 0 = fully hidden, 1 = fully exposed. This is the continuous
 replacement for Epic's binary "seen / not seen".

properties.name: VisiblePointCount
properties.doc: Number of sample points that had a clear line this evaluation. Vision only.

properties.name: DetectedByCone
properties.doc: Which cone produced the detection. Vision only.

properties.name: Blocker
properties.doc:
Why this sense reported nothing, when it reported nothing. Set at each
 early return so "why can't it see me" has an answer instead of a guess.

properties.name: LightLevel
properties.doc:
How lit vision judged the target, 0 (dark) to 1 (fully lit): Light Level Override when
 the target sets one, otherwise the sun-shadow trace or the ambient level. Vision only.
 -1 when vision stopped before judging light (outside the cones, out of range, hidden).

properties.name: bWasActiveLastEval
properties.doc:
What this sense said the last time it was actually asked.

 Senses run on their own intervals — vision every 0.15 s against a 0.05 s
 core tick — so on most ticks a sense has simply not been re-evaluated yet.
 That is not the same as reporting nothing, and belief must not decay while
 waiting for the next evaluation. bIsActive still goes false in the gap, so
 the loss grace timer is unaffected; this is what tells the memory engine to
 hold rather than fade.

properties.name: SubjectKind
properties.doc:
What this belief is about. Actor by default, so every record that existed
 before this field did behaves exactly as it did.

properties.name: SubjectLocation
properties.doc:
Where the subject is, for beliefs with no actor to ask. Meaningless when
 SubjectKind is Actor — read LastKnownPosition there instead.

properties.name: SubjectTag
properties.doc:
What kind of thing this is — "Sound.Gunshot", "Evidence.Body". Empty for
 actor beliefs, which identify themselves.

properties.name: LastSeenCoverActor
properties.doc:
What stood between the AI and the target when it was lost from Detected or
 Tracked — set before On AI Lost fires. Cleared on every loss.

properties.name: LastSeenCoverPosition
properties.doc: Where the line of sight broke, on the face of that cover.

properties.name: LossReason
properties.doc:
Why this target was last lost. Written by MemoryEngine when state → Lost.
Cleared when target is re-detected.
Use in Behavior Trees to drive intelligent search behavior.
See ELossReason comments for recommended BT response per reason.

properties.name: LossDirection
properties.doc:
World direction the target was last moving when lost.
Populated for OutOfRange and ScentLost — useful for predicting where they went.
ZeroVector if direction is unknown.

properties.name: Episodes
properties.doc:
Records of individual past engagements with this target.
Maximum 5 episodes, oldest evicted when full (ring buffer).
Written when target transitions to Lost from Tracked or Detected.
Read via PerceptionCore::GetRecentEpisodes(Target).

Use in BT to ask:
  "Has this target hidden behind that same corner twice?"
  "Did last engagement end with them fleeing or attacking?"
  "How long do engagements with this target typically last?"

properties.name: PrimaryStimulusSource
properties.doc: The source that first made this belief.

properties.name: DominantStimulusSource
properties.doc:
The sense contributing most right now; while none reports, the last source the belief came from (Shared Intel
 for one a squadmate shared). This is what On AI Suspect / On AI Detect pass as Stimulus.

properties.name: TimeSeconds
properties.doc: World seconds at which this was captured.

properties.name: Target
properties.doc: Who the belief was about. May have been destroyed since.

properties.name: Confidence
properties.doc: Confidence as acted on, after smoothing.

properties.name: RawConfidence
properties.doc: Confidence as the senses reported it, before smoothing.

properties.name: LastKnownPosition
properties.doc: Where the AI believed the target was.

properties.name: TimeSinceLastSensed
properties.doc: Seconds since any sense last had this target.

properties.name: ActiveSenseCount
properties.doc: How many senses were contributing.

properties.name: OwnerEyeForward
properties.doc:
Facing the senses should use. Resolved from actor / control / socket rotation
 per the profile's EyeDirectionMode, with optional lag so the cone trails the
 body instead of snapping. Senses should prefer this over OwnerRotation.Vector().

properties.name: bOwnerOffscreen
properties.doc:
True when the owning AI is outside every local player's view frustum.
 Fairness rules use this to make off-screen AI slightly less sensitive.

properties.name: QualityMaxVisionSamples
properties.doc: Cap on vision sample points this evaluation. 0 = use the profile's value.

properties.name: bQualitySkipPerTargetLight
properties.doc:
Skip per-target light sampling and the sun-shadow trace, using the global
 ambient level instead.

properties.name: GraceTime
properties.doc:
Seconds after losing the sense signal before transitioning to Lost.
Brief cover (thin pillar, doorframe) won't immediately drop the target.

Defaults per sense:
  Vision       0.3s  — hide behind wall, gone fast
  Hearing      3.0s  — sound echo lingers
  Touch        0.5s  — lost contact
  Smell        20.0s — scent cloud persists
  Vibration    0.0s  — movement stopped, instant
  Damage       8.0s  — AI remembers being hit
  Echolocation 0.6s  — sonar pulse missed

properties.name: bDirectCut
properties.doc:
If true, AI jumps directly to Lost once grace expires.
If false, confidence decays through each threshold first (slower step-down).

  true  = Vision, Echolocation  (precise — either detecting or not)
  false = Hearing, Smell, Touch, Vibration, Damage  (gradual fade)

properties.name: ConfidenceDecayMultiplier
properties.doc:
Multiplier on base confidence decay rate after this sense goes silent.
1.0 = normal decay. 3.0 = confidence drops 3x faster after losing this sense.
Use higher values for precise senses (Vision), lower for lingering ones (Smell).

properties.name: Tag
properties.doc:
Identity of this evidence. Adding a second entry with the same tag replaces
 the first, so re-applying "Disguise" refreshes it instead of stacking.

properties.name: Value
properties.doc: Meaning depends on Operation. Ignored entirely by Invalidate.

properties.name: Lifetime
properties.doc: Seconds before this expires on its own. 0 or less = holds until removed.

properties.name: Source
properties.doc:
Provenance, for debugging and for later modules that care who said so.
 Free-form: "Disguise", "Dispatch", "Cutscene_03".

properties.name: Age
properties.doc: Seconds this entry has been held. Managed by APS.

properties.name: StimulusTag
properties.doc:
Tag identifying the stimulus type. Uses dot-prefix hierarchy.
Examples: "Stimulus.Sound.Footstep", "Stimulus.Vibration.Blast",
          "Stimulus.Custom.Psychic", "Stimulus.Thermal.Body"
Senses register a prefix to receive all events under that namespace.

properties.name: Location
properties.doc: World origin of the stimulus.

properties.name: Source
properties.doc: Actor that caused the stimulus. May be null for environmental stimuli.

properties.name: Strength
properties.doc: Intensity 0-1. Maps to confidence contribution in the receiving sense.

properties.name: Radius
properties.doc: Detection radius (cm). Agents beyond this distance do not receive the stimulus.

properties.name: MaxLODTier
properties.doc:
Maximum LOD tier that receives this stimulus [0-4].
0 = only very close AI. 4 = all AI regardless of distance.
Match to stimulus importance: footstep=1, gunshot=3, explosion=4.

properties.name: bRequiresClearPath
properties.doc:
True = run a wall occlusion trace before delivering to each agent.
Expensive — only enable for stimuli where geometry matters (sound, heat, light).
False = stimulus passes through walls (vibration, psychic, magnetic).

properties.name: bTeamFilter
properties.doc: True = skip agents on the same team as Source.

properties.name: CrouchRatio
properties.doc: Ratio of ticks player was crouching while AI had vision. 0-1.

properties.name: SprintRatio
properties.doc: Ratio of ticks player was sprinting (speed > SprintThreshold). 0-1.

properties.name: WalkRatio
properties.doc: Ratio of ticks player was walking slowly. 0-1.

properties.name: StealthRatio
properties.doc: Ratio of engagements where player attacked from behind/side vs frontal.

properties.name: AggressionRatio
properties.doc: Ratio of engagements where player charged in vs backed off.

properties.name: RecentHideLocations
properties.doc: Last 5 positions where AI transitioned to Lost (player hid here).

properties.name: CustomBehaviorRatios
properties.doc:
Arbitrary named behavior ratios you define.
Add any key you want from Blueprint or C++ — no recompile needed.
Examples: "UsedCover", "FiredFromDistance", "AlwaysFlankLeft"
Values are 0-1 ratios updated via RecordCustomBehavior().

properties.name: EngagementCount
properties.doc: Number of distinct engagements observed so far.

properties.name: bHasEnoughData
properties.doc:
True once EngagementCount >= MinEngagementsRequired.
AI only adapts its behavior when this is true.

properties.name: TeamRelationships
properties.doc: Map team ID -> relationship. Uses IGenericTeamAgentInterface.

properties.name: ClassRelationships
properties.doc: Map actor class -> relationship override (takes priority over team).

properties.name: DefaultRelationship
properties.doc: Default when no rule matches.

properties.name: DefaultInterval
properties.doc: Seconds between evaluations of this sense. Overridden per-profile by Sense Intervals.

properties.name: MaxSensingRange
properties.doc:
Furthest this sense can reach (cm). Feeds the candidate-gathering radius, so
 a sense that reaches further than vision must say so or its targets are
 never even considered. 0 means it adds nothing to the gather range.

properties.name: LossGraceTime
properties.doc: Seconds of silence before this sense allows the target to be considered lost.

properties.name: bAllowsDirectLostCut
properties.doc:
True = jump straight to Lost once grace expires, the way vision does when a
 target steps behind a wall. False = fade down through the states.

properties.name: SenseLossReason
properties.doc:
Reason written to the belief record when this sense is the one that lost the
 target. Behaviour trees read it to decide how to search.

properties.name: SubscribedStimulusTags
properties.doc:
Stimulus tag prefixes this sense subscribes to. Prefix matched, so
 "Stimulus.Sound" receives "Stimulus.Sound.Gunshot". Empty = opt out.

properties.name: Source
properties.doc: The actor that produced the sound.

properties.name: Loudness
properties.doc:
Scaled loudness.
New path:    BaseLoudness * LoudnessMultiplier (pre-scaled by PerceptionSoundSystem).
Scaled loudness passed from PerceptionSoundSystem.

properties.name: MaxRangeOverride
properties.doc:
Legacy range override (cm). Only used when SoundType is null.
0 = use default fallback range (1500cm).

properties.name: SoundType
properties.doc:
Sound type definition (new path). Null = legacy path.
When set, MaxRange and LocationAccuracyOverride are read from here.

properties.name: bClearPath
properties.doc:
Was there a clear line-of-sound when this event was reported?
Pre-computed by PerceptionSoundSystem to avoid double wall-trace.
Only valid when SoundType is set.

properties.name: bIsLocationSound
properties.doc:
True when emitted via EmitSoundAtLocation — no source actor.
SoundLocation holds the world position. Source is null.

properties.name: SoundLocation
properties.doc: World position for location-based sounds (used when bIsLocationSound=true).

properties.name: PainLevels
properties.doc:
Modular pain types — keyed directly on DataAsset pointer (no FName ID needed).
UPROPERTYs so garbage collection sees the assets they point at: a pain asset
loaded on demand and later released would otherwise leave a dangling key that
GetSenseDegradation dereferences every tick.

properties.name: PreviousPainLevels
properties.doc: previous level

properties.name: DisabledPainTypes
properties.doc: types turned off by SetPainTypeEnabledFromDefinition

properties.name: PendingPainReports
properties.doc:
Pending OnAIPainReported payloads. A queue, not a single slot: several reports
between two perception passes — a shotgun blast, then the fire it starts —
each get their own event, carrying the level as it stood after that report.

properties.name: MaxSmellRange
properties.doc:
Maximum range at which this sense can detect targets (cm).
Much shorter than vision or hearing; smell is close-range.

properties.name: WindDirection
properties.doc:
The way the wind blows, in world space (normalized XY vector) — the direction
the air moves, as a weathervane's tail points. ZeroVector = use the world's
wind (Set Wind State on the APS subsystem, or an APS Environment volume).
A target is "upwind" when it is in the direction the wind is blowing FROM.
Example: WindDirection = (1, 0, 0) means wind blows in +X direction,
  so a target at -X is upwind and its scent drifts +X toward the perceiver.

properties.name: DownwindBonus
properties.doc:
Multiplier applied when perceiver is downwind of target (maximum scent strength).
Range [1.0 .. 3.0]. Default 2.0 = scent is twice as strong when perfectly downwind.

properties.name: BaseScentIntensity
properties.doc:
Base scent intensity of targets. Increase for "strongly scented" targets
(animals, sewage, explosives) or reduce for neutral/masked targets.
This is the noise equivalent for smell: higher = easier to detect.

properties.name: ScentThreshold
properties.doc:
Minimum scent intensity required to register a detection.
Acts like HearingBaseThreshold. Lower = more sensitive.

properties.name: WallAbsorptionCoeff
properties.doc:
Absorption per wall crossing. Walls partially block scent (lower than hearing by default,
since scent can seep under doors).

properties.name: SmellAccumulationRate
properties.doc: How fast scent confidence builds per second when target is in range.

properties.name: SmellAccumulationDecayRate
properties.doc: How fast scent confidence decays per second when target leaves range.

properties.name: Strength
properties.doc: Strength 0-1. Derived from physics impulse or set manually.

properties.name: ContactLocation
properties.doc: World location of the contact point.

properties.name: Duration
properties.doc: Duration this contact has been active (seconds). Updated each tick while still in contact.

properties.name: bPersistent
properties.doc: True = contact is ongoing (overlap). False = one-shot hit.

properties.name: MaxImpulseForFullStrength
properties.doc: Impulse magnitude that maps to Strength=1.0. Scale to your game's physics units.

properties.name: ContactTypeStrengthMultiplier
properties.doc: Confidence multiplier per contact type. Lets you tune impact per type in the asset.

properties.name: PersistentAccumulationRate
properties.doc:
How fast persistent contact confidence builds per second.
Grab held for 2s at AccumulationRate=0.3 → 0.6 accumulated confidence bonus.

properties.name: MaxPersistentBonus
properties.doc: Max accumulated confidence bonus from persistent contact.

properties.name: BaseLoudness
properties.doc: Base loudness. 1.0=normal footstep, 3.0=gunshot, 0.3=whisper.

properties.name: MaxRange
properties.doc: Max detection range (cm). Footstep=800, Gunshot=4000, Explosion=10000.

properties.name: bIsDirectional
properties.doc: True = AI knows exact direction. False = vague direction only.

properties.name: LocationAccuracyOverride
properties.doc: Location accuracy [0-1]. 0.0=use default formula. 0.9=very precise (gunshot). 0.2=vague.

properties.name: Priority
properties.doc: Priority [0-10]. Higher wins when sound budget is full. Explosion=10, Footstep=1.

properties.name: MaxLODTier
properties.doc:
Max LOD tier that hears this sound [0-4].
Footstep=1 (close AI only), Gunshot=3 (most AI), Explosion=4 (all AI hear it).
Prevents processing quiet sounds for distant AI agents.

properties.name: MaxPendingPerTick
properties.doc: Max sounds of this type queued per AI per tick. Prevents array bloat.

properties.name: bEnabled
properties.doc: False = hear everything. True = apply filters below.

properties.name: AcceptedCategories
properties.doc: Sound categories this AI reacts to. Empty list = completely deaf.

properties.name: MinAlertLevel
properties.doc:
Minimum alert level. Whisper=react to all sounds.
Loud=only gunshots+. Explosive=only explosions.

properties.name: LoudnessMultiplier
properties.doc: Loudness multiplier. 1.0=normal, 2.0=sensitive ears (dog), 0.5=hard of hearing.

properties.name: bFilterFriendlyTeam
properties.doc:
True = ignore sounds from the same team. Uses IGenericTeamAgentInterface,
 read from the actor itself or else from its controller (or, for a
 projectile, from whoever launched it).

properties.name: EvidenceTag
properties.doc:
What kind of trace this is — "Body", "Blood", "ForcedLock", "Footprints".
 Your vocabulary; the plugin attaches no meaning to any of them.

properties.name: Conspicuousness
properties.doc:
How obvious this is [0..1]. 1 is a body in a corridor; 0.2 is a scuff mark.

An observer must perceive it at least this well before it registers, so
subtle traces need a closer, longer look — and a hurried search misses them,
which is the behaviour that makes searching feel like searching.

properties.name: BeliefStrength
properties.doc:
How strongly discovering this should register, [0..1]. Feeds the confidence
 of the location belief it produces.

properties.name: LifetimeSeconds
properties.doc:
Seconds before this fades from the world on its own. 0 = it stays until
 something removes it. Blood dries; a body does not tidy itself away.

properties.name: Instigator
properties.doc:
Who caused it, if the game knows. Carried into the finder's memory, so
 "this was them" is available without the AI having witnessed anything.

properties.name: ImpliedDirection
properties.doc: Which way it suggests they went. Zero when it says nothing about direction.

properties.name: bAutoRegisterAsPerceivable
properties.doc:
Register this actor as perceivable on BeginPlay, so AI can find it with no
 further setup. Turn off if your project registers it another way.

properties.name: Delay
properties.doc:
Seconds before the faction knows. The window in which stopping the
 messenger still changes the outcome.

properties.name: PositionError
properties.doc: Random position error added, in cm. A shouted location is approximate.

properties.name: TraitLossChance
properties.doc:
Chance per trait that a detail is lost in the retelling [0..1]. Weighted by
 observability, so the obvious things survive and the subtle ones do not.

properties.name: ConfidenceScale
properties.doc: Multiplier on the reported confidence. Second-hand is less certain.

properties.name: Subject
properties.doc:
The actor this is about, when anyone has actually identified one. Null for
 a description nobody has tied to a person yet — which is the normal state
 of a manhunt before it succeeds.

properties.name: Descriptor
properties.doc: What is known about them.

properties.name: Age
properties.doc: Seconds since this was last refreshed by anyone.

properties.name: Provenance
properties.doc: Who said so. Free-form: an agent's name, "Dispatch", "Camera_03".

properties.name: HopCount
properties.doc: How many retellings from the original sighting. 0 means witnessed.

properties.name: EntryDecayPerSecond
properties.doc: Confidence lost per second while nobody refreshes an entry.

properties.name: EntryForgetThreshold
properties.doc: Below this, the faction stops believing it and the entry is dropped.

properties.name: AlertDecayPerSecond
properties.doc: Alert lost per second with nothing new coming in.

properties.name: MergeMatchThreshold
properties.doc:
How well a description must fit an existing entry to be treated as the same
 person. Too low and unrelated suspects merge; too high and every sighting
 starts a new manhunt.

properties.name: ChannelSpecs
properties.doc: Per-channel costs. Edit to retune how information degrades in transit.

properties.name: Faction
properties.doc:
Who this AI reports to. Entries are scoped per faction, so two factions
 hunting the same person do not share what they have worked out.

properties.name: ReportChannel
properties.doc:
How reports travel. Direct is instant and complete; anything else costs
 time and detail, and can be cut off before it lands.

properties.name: MinConfidenceToReport
properties.doc:
Belief required before this AI is willing to say anything. Below it, the
 AI has a suspicion rather than a sighting.

properties.name: ReportInterval
properties.doc:
Seconds between reports about the same target, so a sustained sighting is
 an update rather than a flood.

properties.name: IdealObservationRange
properties.doc:
Distance at which a look is as good as it gets (cm). Closer than this adds
 nothing; further degrades toward noticing only the obvious.

properties.name: MaxObservationRange
properties.doc: Beyond this, no describable detail is made out at all (cm).

properties.name: AlertPerReport
properties.doc: Alert added to the faction each time this AI files a report.

properties.name: bDiscoverEvidence
properties.doc:
Notice traces left in the world — bodies, blood, forced locks. Off makes
 this AI blind to evidence without changing anything else it does.

properties.name: bReportEvidenceToFaction
properties.doc:
Also file evidence with the faction. Off keeps the discovery private to the
 AI that found it — it knows, its organisation does not.

properties.name: Probability
properties.doc: How likely the target is here, relative to the other points [0..1].

properties.name: DistanceFromSearcher
properties.doc:
Distance from the searcher. Exposed so a caller can trade "most likely"
 against "nearest" itself rather than accepting a ranking it did not choose.

properties.name: CellSize
properties.doc: Grid resolution in cm. Smaller is more precise and costs more cells.

properties.name: GridRadius
properties.doc: Half-width of the grid in cells. 20 at 300 cm covers a 120 m square.

properties.name: TargetSpeed
properties.doc:
How fast the target is assumed able to move, cm/s. This is what turns
 elapsed time into a search area — set it near your player's sprint speed.

properties.name: ClearRadius
properties.doc: How close the searcher must get before a cell counts as checked (cm).

properties.name: bRequireNavigable
properties.doc:
Reject cells that are not on the navmesh, and hand out only places the
searcher can walk to.

This is what stops the search spreading through walls. Each point is the
cell's spot on the navmesh, never its raw centre (which can be inside a wall),
and the first time a point comes up APS checks the searcher has a full path
to it: a closed room or a roof is skipped. Turned off — or with no navigation
system present — every cell is accepted, which degrades to a plain expanding
area rather than failing outright: a project with no navmesh should still get
a usable search, not an empty one.

properties.name: Signature
properties.doc:
The traits an observer can perceive, subject to how good a look they got.

Ships with a plausible starter set so the component does something the
moment it is added. Replace the values with your own.

properties.name: Key
properties.doc: What kind of fact this is — "Clothing", "Vehicle", "Build", "Voice", "Face".

properties.name: Value
properties.doc: The value for this observer to match on — "RedCoat", "BlueSedan", "Tall".

properties.name: Observability
properties.doc:
How easily this is noticed [0..1]. 1 is unmissable at any range a target can
be seen at; 0.1 needs a close, clear look.

Suggested: clothing colour 0.9, build 0.8, vehicle 0.85, gait 0.4,
face 0.25, voice 0.3 (and only when in earshot).

console.name: aps.Visualizer
console.help: What the APS Visualizer shows. 0: nothing. 1 (default): everything. 2: status only (each AI's state over its head).

console.name: aps.VisualizerPage
console.help: The page the APS Visualizer's screen panel shows (0 Senses, 1 Memory, 2 Brain, 3 Squad, 4 Events, 5 Player Model, 6 Environment).

console.name: aps.UseSpatialIndex
console.help: 1 (default): find perception candidates through the APS subsystem's spatial index. 0: fall back to scanning every Pawn in the world, once per agent, per gather.

console.name: aps.Tune
console.help: aps.Tune <PropertyName> <Value> — set a profile value on every running agent, without touching the asset. Try: aps.Tune VisionMaxRange 5000

plugin.Description: APS: belief-based AI perception for UE5. 8 senses fused into one confidence value per target, with beliefs about places as well as actors, spatial memory, loss reasons, threat and emotion modelling, Blueprint-overridable decision policies, and the APS Visualizer: a Blueprint view of what each AI sees, hears and believes, built from APS's own data nodes. Optional Knowledge module adds trait-based identity, faction memory and dispatch. Blueprint-first.
